meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session 5/05/2020
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Work Session Chair Steve Unruhe, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its May 5, 2020 virtual work session, hearing a Strategic Plan Priority 5 operational services update covering ASBO financial reporting recognition, delayed HR/finance software upgrades, custodial benchmarks, NC State transportation efficiency research, and $500 million in prioritized facility needs awaiting county funding. The board unanimously approved (7-0) a $280,000 engineering design commissioning contract for Northern High School by roll-call vote after Minnie Forte-Brown joined the meeting, while earlier approving the agenda (6-0) and April 9 work session minutes (6-0). Academic Services presented plans for virtual, drive-in (at Southpoint Mall), and drive-through 2020 high school graduation ceremonies, alongside a preliminary 1:1 technology and connectivity plan estimating $9.63 million for K-12 (or $6.73 million for grades 3-12) to acquire roughly 19,150 devices and hotspots with support from CARES Act funds and a planned $4 million DPS Foundation fundraising campaign. Administration also outlined an expanded COVID-19 Reentry Task Force addressing year-round calendars, early/middle colleges, and CDC reopening guidance, before the board entered closed session (6-0 after Minnie Forte-Brown departed) and unanimously approved (6-0) the May 7, 2020 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Agenda Approval, and Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Work Session Chair Steve Unruhe called the virtual work session to order and led a moment of silence remembering loved ones and children experiencing hunger during the pandemic. With Minnie Forte-Brown not yet present, the six seated members approved the agenda by roll call (6-0) on a motion by Natalie Beyer seconded by Matt Sears, and approved the April 9, 2020 work session minutes by roll call (6-0) on a motion by Matt Sears seconded by Dr. Mike Lee.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services and Strategic Plan Priority 5 Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Operational Services and Finance staff reported meeting audit and ASBO transparency goals while noting that a new HR/finance software system was delayed three to five years due to state budget and COVID-19 pressures. Staff reviewed custodial inspection improvements, a Clean School Award scorecard, and collaboration with Matthew Palmer and NC State researchers to reduce bus ride times and traffic congestion, while board members asked about class-size funding from the General Assembly and the status of the $500 million prioritized capital list sent to the County Commissioners.

agenda_items.title: Northern High School Commissioning Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk presented a $280,000 commissioning engineering contract covering design-phase review and post-construction testing of mechanical and energy systems through project close-out for the new Northern High School. With Minnie Forte-Brown having joined the call and confirming she heard the discussion, Natalie Beyer moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded approval, which passed 7-0 by roll call.

agenda_items.title: 2020 Graduation Ceremonies Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and graduation coordinator Janet Bell-Parnell outlined plans developed with principals and the Superintendent's Student Advisory for virtual, drive-in (at Southpoint Mall), drive-through, and combined livestreamed ceremonies, supplemented by yard signs delivered to all seniors. Board members asked about school-level decision autonomy, PPE and social distancing enforcement, weather contingencies for rain versus lightning, and potential venue cost savings from not using Duke University or NCCU.

agenda_items.title: 1:1 Technology and Connectivity Plan Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy, Paul Majumbi, Chanel Sidbury, and Tanya Giovanni presented preliminary estimates from the 36-member 1:1 Device Committee, showing ~19,150 devices needed across DPS (totaling $9.63 million with hotspots for K-12 or $6.73 million for grades 3-12 at ~$360.75 per Lenovo Chromebook). Board members pressed for volume discounts, lease-versus-purchase options (noting CARES Act spending deadlines favor purchasing), Learning Management System alignment, EC/CTE device needs, and coordination with a $4 million DPS Foundation fundraising campaign ahead of a formal June plan.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Reentry Task Force Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and Dr. Pascal Mubenga presented the expanded COVID-19 Reentry Task Force covering calendars, enrollment, illness management, cleaning, gatherings, and transportation, noting a recommendation on year-round schools would return in two weeks while early/middle colleges would follow partner university schedules. Board members urged adding parent physicians/public health experts, expanding EC representation, gathering family feedback, and organizing the large task force into focused work groups.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and May 7, 2020 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: With Minnie Forte-Brown having departed earlier, the six remaining members voted 6-0 by roll call to enter closed session. Returning to open session at 02:39:41, the board approved the personnel report dated May 7, 2020 by a 6-0 roll-call vote on a motion by Matt Sears seconded by Bettina Umstead before Chair Unruhe offered Teacher Appreciation Week remarks and adjourned.

meetings.title: Board of Education Retreat April 30, 2020
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee presided over the Board of Education's annual retreat on April 30, 2020, conducted virtually alongside Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga, staff, incoming board members, and community Sounding Board advisors to lay the groundwork for comprehensive student assignment and boundary redistricting. Dr. Kelvin Bullock presented historical demographic trends showing DPS has no single racial majority, serves >75% students of color in 74% of its schools, and experienced a 3,058-student decline in Black enrollment alongside a 3,492-student rise in Latinx enrollment over eight years. Matthew Palmer reported updated 10-year enrollment projections rising from 32,430 to 34,894 students, an existing 189-seat elementary capacity deficit, and uneven regional distribution of Pre-K and Exceptional Children classrooms, while Melody Marshall and Kimberly Lane audited Policy 4150 and magnet schools—finding steep declines in available magnet lottery seats since K-3 class size caps and wide demographic/socioeconomic disparities across schools. Mary Filardo of the 21st Century School Fund demonstrated a census-block boundary planning dashboard, and the board informally endorsed proceeding with small-group community engagement while taking no formal votes.

agenda_items.title: Opening Welcome, Sounding Board Introductions, and Connection Exercise
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Dr. Mike Lee and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga opened the annual retreat, welcoming incoming board members and community Sounding Board advisors including Dr. Priddy and Antonio Jones. Each board member spent roughly 45 seconds reflecting on a photograph of DPS students downtown under the moon to reconnect before technical presentations began.

agenda_items.title: Capital Projects, McDougald Terrace / Morehead Relocation, and Boundary Planning Context
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reviewed elementary capital additions, support for displaced McDougald Terrace families, the temporary relocation of Morehead Montessori to Hope Valley Elementary, and the six months of preparation since November board action to examine student assignment policies and 90-minute transportation ride times. Board members emphasized centering an equity lens, using national models, and ensuring broad community engagement across all corners of Durham.

agenda_items.title: Historical Enrollment and Demographic Trends
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Kelvin Bullock traced DPS demographic shifts from 1993 through 2020, highlighting that 74% of schools serve over 75% students of color, Black student enrollment fell by 3,058 over eight years while Latinx enrollment grew by 3,492, and 38% of schools exceed 75% free/reduced lunch eligibility. Board members thanked Dr. Bullock for framing serving students of color as a privilege and asked for countywide school-age population comparisons and teacher-experience equity data.

agenda_items.title: Enrollment Projections and Elementary Capacity Analysis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Matthew Palmer presented updated 10-year enrollment projections increasing from 32,430 (projected 18 months earlier) to 34,894 students due to residential growth in eastern Durham and recent enrollment gains, noting DPS currently has a 189-seat elementary deficit (including ~450 seats short in the Jordan region). He also highlighted uneven regional clustering of Pre-K and Exceptional Children classrooms and urged integrating middle school feeder alignment as planning progresses.

agenda_items.title: Policy 4150 Review, Magnet Priorities, and Elementary School Equity Audit
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Deborah Pittman, Melody Marshall, and Kimberly Lane reviewed Policy 4150's complex priority rules across 23 magnet schools (14 filled by lottery), showing magnet applications jumped 58% while available seats fell sharply after state K-3 class size limits. School-by-school data revealed stark disparities in free/reduced lunch rates (26% to 99%), minority group isolation, and magnet concentration (four elementary magnets in Hillside's zone versus zero in Southern's), prompting board discussion on whether magnets should reflect district or countywide demographics and noting a pending Duke Behavioral Science school-choice study.

agenda_items.title: Boundary Planning Dashboard Demonstration and Community Engagement Next Steps
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mary Filardo of the 21st Century School Fund demonstrated an interactive census-block boundary planning tool mapping student demographics, capacity, and charter enrollment across scenarios (protected by permission controls until public rollout). Staff outlined a coalition-building community engagement strategy beyond traditional PTAs, and Chairman Dr. Mike Lee gave informal concurrence to proceed with small-group briefings before adjourning at 04:37:30.

meetings.title: Durham Board of Education Monthly Meeting April 23, 2020  6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee presided over the April 23, 2020 virtual monthly meeting, where the board amended the agenda (7-0) to recognize March and April Students of the Month, heard an update on COVID-19 state grading guidance and $11.2M–$12.6M in projected federal CARES Act relief, and logged 97 written public comments on Exceptional Children reorganization, Riverside High School technology access, and COVID-19 operations. Following unanimous approval (7-0) of the consent agenda and 2020-21 E-Rate applications totaling $2,170,870 (80% federal discount), the board approved Policy 7300 (employee recording language) on second reading by a 6-1 vote, with Dr. Mike Lee, Bettina Umstead, Natalie Beyer, Minnie Forte-Brown, Xavier Cason, and Steve Unruhe voting Aye and Matt Sears voting Nay. In the evening's main instructional decision, after Minnie Forte-Brown argued for following the teacher-voted matrix of Houghton Mifflin Harcourt Into Reading and McGraw-Hill Wonders while Matt Sears, Natalie Beyer, Steve Unruhe, and Xavier Cason favored Into Reading paired with American Reading Company (ARC), the board unanimously adopted (7-0) Into Reading and ARC before entering closed session (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Amendment for Student Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the meeting to order and led a moment of silence for students coping with stay-at-home stress and missing teachers, cafeteria workers, and custodians. Xavier Cason moved and Natalie Beyer seconded amending the agenda to celebrate March and April Students of the Month prior to the superintendent's update, passing 7-0 by show of hands.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's COVID-19 Update, Agenda Approval, and Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga and finance/academic staff reported new State Board grading guidance, a partnership with Food Insight Group and restaurants for Durham FEAST meals, ~$240,000 in phase-two packet mailing costs, $850,000 in state COVID funds, and an estimated $11.2M–$12.6M in federal CARES Act funds, plus plans to align with the state's 22-credit graduation waiver. The board then unanimously approved (7-0) the full agenda and the March 26, 2020 minutes.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment (97 Written Submissions)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because 97 written public comments were submitted, Chief Communications Officer Chip Sudderth categorized the submissions and read all 97 commenter names aloud rather than reading texts in full, covering EC reorganization/services, COVID-19 distancing/safety, K-5 literacy adoption, and technology access (primarily from the Riverside High School community). Steve Unruhe urged posting all comments online immediately after any required privacy redactions.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved (7-0) the four-item consent agenda containing the Policy 7000A series on second reading, the quarterly change order report, the Durham Technical Community College articulation agreement, and the graduation policy waiver.

agenda_items.title: Policy 7300 (Staff Responsibilities and Code of Ethics) Second Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni presented reordered and clarified Policy 7300 employee recording language drafted by counsel to address prior board concerns about chilling official-business recordings. Natalie Beyer praised the revision, and the board approved Policy 7300 on second reading by a 6-1 vote with Matt Sears dissenting.

agenda_items.title: 2020-21 E-Rate Applications and Contracts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: IT Executive Director Benjamin Brown presented 2020-21 E-Rate Category 1 and Category 2 applications totaling $2,170,870 at an 80% discount (~$434,174 local match), including a three-year Spectrum 10-Gbps WAN contract at $750/month per school ($5 cheaper than prior 1-Gbps service) and $1.4M to replace end-of-life switches. The board approved the applications and contracts 7-0.

agenda_items.title: K-5 Elementary Literacy Core Curriculum Adoption
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and Chanel Sidbury presented the K-5 literacy adoption recommendation based on first- and second-choice school votes favoring Houghton Mifflin Harcourt Into Reading and McGraw-Hill Wonders. After debate over Wonders' failing social justice scorecard rating versus American Reading Company's (ARC) higher cost and pedagogical differentiation, Xavier Cason moved approval of Into Reading and ARC, which passed unanimously (7-0) with Dr. Mubenga noting other budget cuts would be evaluated to cover costs.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously (7-0) to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda and adjourned at 02:27:17.

votes.notes: Hand vote conducted via Zoom; chair confirmed Matt Sears's affirmative vote verbally.
votes.discussion_detail: Added Student of the Month celebrations for March and April ahead of the Superintendent's update.

votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the full monthly meeting agenda following the superintendent's update.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved the minutes of the March 26, 2020 monthly meeting.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Board of Education Monthly Meeting April 23, 2020  6:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Policy 7300 Employee Recording Restrictions (Second Reading)
disagreements.summary: While six board members accepted legal counsel's reordered Policy 7300 language regulating employee recordings on school property, Matt Sears dissented in a 6-1 vote.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt revised Policy 7300 prohibiting secret one-party employee recordings while clarifying exceptions for approved curriculum and official business.
side_a_arguments: Reordering the clauses removes the chilling opening language identified at the April 9 work session.
Explicitly protects teachers and staff making approved instructional recordings.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose adopting Policy 7300 as drafted.
side_b_arguments: Recorded a dissenting vote against the policy on second reading.
disagreements.resolution: Policy 7300 passed 6-1 on second reading with Matt Sears dissenting.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Board of Education Monthly Meeting April 23, 2020  6:30 PM
disagreements.issue: K-5 Literacy Core Curriculum Selection: Into Reading + ARC vs. Into Reading + Wonders
disagreements.summary: Board members debated whether to adopt the staff-recommended combination of Houghton Mifflin Harcourt Into Reading and McGraw-Hill Wonders based on combined first- and second-choice school votes, or pair Into Reading with American Reading Company (ARC) despite higher cost.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt Into Reading and American Reading Company (ARC) to provide two qualitatively distinct curriculum options and avoid Wonders' cultural responsiveness deficiencies.
side_a_arguments: ARC tied Into Reading in first-choice school votes and offers a qualitatively different instructional model than two similar basal readers.
McGraw-Hill Wonders was rated culturally insufficient on social justice and required supplemental purchases.
Investing in K-5 literacy is a top priority second only to universal Pre-K, even if future budget trade-offs are required.
disagreements.side_b_position: Follow the school vote matrix recommending Into Reading and Wonders, warning that ARC costs more and could squeeze funds for Pre-K or other priorities.
side_b_arguments: Teachers voted under an agreed first- and second-choice ranking process and deserve to see their combined vote honored.
ARC's higher cost could force cuts in other areas such as AIG or Pre-K if county funds are constrained.
disagreements.resolution: Xavier Cason moved to adopt Into Reading and ARC, and Minnie Forte-Brown joined the board in passing the motion 7-0 while urging county support for Pre-K.

meetings.title: Durham Board of Education Work Session April 9, 2020  5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Work Session Chair Xavier Cason presided over the April 9, 2020 virtual work session, where the board unanimously approved (7-0) the amended agenda, March 12 work session minutes, and consent items, and authorized issuing an RFP to replace audit firm Rives & Associates (7-0) amid reported management lawsuits. Following board objections from Steve Unruhe and Natalie Beyer over overly broad one-party recording bans in Policy 7300, the board voted 7-0 to advance the remaining Policy 7000A series to consent while holding Policy 7300 for revised language. A sharp policy debate emerged over the K-5 elementary literacy curriculum adoption: Minnie Forte-Brown urged immediately approving the teacher-ranked Houghton Mifflin Harcourt Into Reading and McGraw-Hill Wonders package, whereas Matt Sears, Natalie Beyer, Steve Unruhe, and Bettina Umstead raised concerns about pandemic fiscal uncertainty, Wonders' failing social justice scorecard, and strong school interest in American Reading Company (ARC), resulting in a two-week deferral for comparative cost and scorecard data. After Operational Services presented custodial program needs and COVID-19 emergency leave/feeding disruptions—and Dr. Mike Lee signed off early for his birthday—the remaining six members voted 6-0 to enter closed session, approve the amended April 9 personnel report (6-0), and authorize the chair to sign a COVID-19 resolution (6-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Amendment, Minutes, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Xavier Cason opened the meeting with a moment of silence and entertained an agenda amendment moved by Dr. Mike Lee and seconded by Steve Unruhe to add a discussion of audit firm Rives & Associates under Operational Services (passed 7-0). The board then unanimously approved (7-0) the March 12, 2020 work session minutes and the two consent items (Community Schools District Coordinator position and FY 2019-20 budget adjustment), and noted public comments would be posted online.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda amendment passed 7-0; Minutes passed 7-0; Consent passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: Policy 7000A Series First Reading and Policy 7300 Recording Restrictions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni presented the Policy 7000A personnel transition series. Steve Unruhe and Natalie Beyer objected that proposed one-party recording language in Policy 7300 was too restrictive and could chill official-business or student recordings, prompting a 7-0 vote to place the rest of the 7000A policies on the April consent agenda while returning Policy 7300 with revised wording.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: In-House Custodial Program Deep-Dive
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk, Travis Anderson, Ralph, and Alex Modestou reviewed the first year of transitioning custodial services back in-house, detailing square-footage staffing deficits at Level 3 versus strategic-plan Level 2 standards, summer deep-clean constraints with 10-month part-time staff, night-shift supervision needs, laundry facilities, workers' compensation risks, and plans to standardize facility rental fees to recover real costs. Board members raised asthma/air quality, stair tread safety, biweekly pay for hourly workers, and preserving community access philosophy when revising rental rates.

agenda_items.title: Audit Firm Contract (Rives & Associates) RFP Authorization
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Paul LeSieur reported that audit firm Rives & Associates faced management-related lawsuits and other NC districts were issuing RFPs, noting DPS had not yet signed an audit contract for FY 2019-20. On a motion by Dr. Mike Lee seconded by Natalie Beyer, the board voted 7-0 to authorize issuing a competitive bid process for a new audit firm.

agenda_items.title: K-5 Elementary Literacy Core Curriculum Recommendation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and Chanel Sidbury recommended adopting Houghton Mifflin Harcourt Into Reading and McGraw-Hill Wonders (plus Scholastic supplements) on an extended five-year payment schedule (~$603,000/year) based on combined first- and second-choice school votes. Minnie Forte-Brown pushed for an immediate vote honoring teachers' rankings, while Matt Sears, Natalie Beyer, Steve Unruhe, and Bettina Umstead cited COVID-19 fiscal uncertainty, Wonders' failing social justice scorecard, and tied first-place support for ARC; the board agreed by consensus to defer the vote two weeks for cost and scorecard comparisons across all three options.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Operations, Leave, Feeding Program, and Ignite Grading Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported a $200,000 Duke Endowment device grant, over 850–1,000 state emergency paid leave requests causing school nutrition, custodial, and bus driver staffing shortages (forcing a shift to DPS Foundation/restaurant meal partnerships), ~$330,000 in initial COVID expenses covered by PRC 154 and CARES funds, and the Ignite remote learning/no-harm grading framework. Dr. Mike Lee signed off at 03:14:36 after birthday wishes from the board.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session, Amended Personnel Report, and COVID-19 Board Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The six remaining members voted 6-0 to enter closed session and reconvened at 03:50:15 to approve the amended April 9, 2020 personnel report (6-0) on a motion by Natalie Beyer. Before adjourning, Minnie Forte-Brown moved and Steve Unruhe seconded authorizing the board chair to sign the board's COVID-19 resolution, passing 6-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Board of Education Work Session April 9, 2020  5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Policy 7300 Prohibition on One-Party Employee Recordings
disagreements.summary: Board members challenged proposed Policy 7300 language barring one-party employee recordings on school property without principal/supervisor permission as overly broad and potentially chilling official-business recordings.
disagreements.side_a_position: Prohibit secret one-party recordings to ensure staff and coworkers feel safe from unfair covert recording.
side_a_arguments: Secret recordings can chill candid workplace conversations among supervisors and staff.
disagreements.side_b_position: Narrow the prohibition to secret recordings and explicitly protect official-business and instructional recordings.
side_b_arguments: Barring recordings without supervisor/principal permission is too restrictive and does not clearly protect official business.
disagreements.resolution: Board voted 7-0 to advance the other 7000A policies to consent while returning Policy 7300 with revised wording at the April 23 meeting.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Board of Education Work Session April 9, 2020  5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Timing and Choice of K-5 Literacy Core Curriculum Adoption
disagreements.summary: Board members split over whether to immediately adopt staff's recommendation of Houghton Mifflin Harcourt Into Reading plus McGraw-Hill Wonders or defer two weeks to evaluate American Reading Company (ARC), single-vendor costs, and cultural responsiveness scorecards.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt Into Reading and Wonders immediately to honor teacher votes, maintain instructional momentum, and avoid ARC's ~$950,000 higher price tag.
side_a_arguments: Teachers voted under the agreed first- and second-choice process, and rejecting their choice undermines trust and accountability.
Further delay risks failing to have standardized literacy materials ready for the fall when proficiency is already under 50%.
ARC costs roughly $950,000 more, and specialists can supplement Wonders' social justice gaps.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer the vote two weeks to review scorecards and multi-year pricing for all three curricula (including ARC and single-curriculum options) amid COVID-19 budget uncertainty.
side_b_arguments: Into Reading and Wonders are very similar basal readers while ARC tied for first-choice votes (10 each) and offers a distinct approach.
Wonders scored culturally insufficient on social justice, requiring supplemental materials.
A looming pandemic recession and potential state revenue shortfalls require scrutinizing multi-year financial commitments and single-vendor pricing.
disagreements.resolution: Board agreed by consensus at 02:56:11 to defer the decision two weeks to April 23 and requested full scorecards and cost comparisons.

meetings.title: Durham Board of Education Monthly Meeting March 26, 2020  6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: In its first fully virtual Zoom meeting on March 26, 2020, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education (presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, with Vice Chair Bettina Umstead briefly filling in during an audio drop) opened with a moment of silence for COVID-19 impacts and the passing of State Representative Mary Ann Black before hearing updates on meal delivery, remote learning packets, and early enactment of federal emergency paid sick leave and expanded FMLA. After Chip Sudderth read 38+ minutes of submitted public comments from teachers, custodians, and parents demanding workplace safety, classified pay protections, and clearer remote learning/grading guidance, the board unanimously approved (7-0) the amended agenda, February 27 minutes, and a five-item consent agenda including Policy 4000B second reading and land purchase adjoining Elementary School C. A major disagreement emerged over the FY 2020-21 county budget request: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga and CFO Paul LeSieur proposed cutting $3.1 million—deferring the $15/hour classified minimum wage and $1.4 million in teacher salary supplements—which Dr. Mike Lee initially defended as fiscally prudent, while Minnie Forte-Brown refused to vote for the cuts and was joined by Xavier Cason, Bettina Umstead, and Steve Unruhe in demanding full restoration plus counselor additions. The board resolved the dispute unanimously (7-0), adopting an amended FY 2020-21 local budget request totaling $19.38 million (including charter school pass-through) and agreeing by consensus to draft a state resolution seeking emergency pay protections for classified staff.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Superintendent's COVID-19 Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened the board's first Zoom meeting with a moment of silence for COVID-19 impacts, essential workers, and State Representative Mary Ann Black. Dr. Pascal Mubenga, Dr. Julius Monk, Marissa Atkins, and Dr. Nakia Hardy updated the board on meal distribution at McDougald Terrace hotel sites, Phase 2/3 instructional packets, state grading plans under the closure through May 15, and implementing federal emergency paid sick leave and FMLA early on March 30.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Due to an audio drop for Chair Lee, Vice Chair Bettina Umstead introduced public comment as Chief Communications Officer Chip Sudderth read submitted comments aloud for one minute each through 01:25:37. Speakers included teachers, parents, and custodial/classified employees raising urgent concerns about custodian safety while disinfecting closed schools, continuing pay for hourly staff, equity in remote learning, and senior graduation.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval, February 27 Minutes, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Rejoining with restored audio, Chair Dr. Mike Lee led a 7-0 hand vote (moved by Xavier Cason, seconded by Steve Unruhe) adding discussion of the superintendent's COVID-19 update ahead of the budget, followed by 7-0 approval of the February 27 minutes (Beyer/Umstead). The board then approved the five-item consent agenda 7-0 (Beyer/Sears), covering Policy 4000B second reading, Parkwood Elementary mobile classrooms, Little River roof lottery application, 1.75 acres at 904/840 Scott King Road adjoining Elementary School C, and Summer Learning.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda passed 7-0; Minutes passed 7-0; Consent passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: Board Discussion of COVID-19 Operations, Leave, and Remote Learning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members questioned staff attendance rates (58% custodial, 66% nutrition, 75% bus drivers), PPE supplies, and inconsistent principal expectations for teachers and hourly workers. Matt Sears and Xavier Cason urged pausing business-as-usual academic pressures to prioritize food, income security, and equity; Minnie Forte-Brown called for clear daily schedules and consistent messaging; and Bettina Umstead, Natalie Beyer, and Dr. Lee backed drafting a board resolution urging state lawmakers to guarantee pay for classified workers unable to work remotely.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Proposed FY 2020-21 County Budget Request
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga and CFO Paul LeSieur presented a pandemic-adjusted $14.3 million county budget request that deferred $3.1 million for the $15/hour classified minimum wage and $1.4 million in teacher salary supplements, plus other deferred instructional support items. After Minnie Forte-Brown refused to vote for the cuts and Xavier Cason, Bettina Umstead, and Steve Unruhe backed restoring the items and adding counselor positions, the board voted 7-0 (moved by Bettina Umstead, seconded by Natalie Beyer) to approve an amended FY 2020-21 request restoring the $15 minimum wage, teacher supplements, and counselors—bringing the total county ask to $19.38 million including charter pass-through.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Board of Education Monthly Meeting March 26, 2020  6:30 PM
disagreements.issue: FY 2020-21 County Budget Request: COVID-19 Austerity Reductions vs. Restoring $15 Minimum Wage, Teacher Supplements, and Counselors
disagreements.summary: Administration proposed trimming the FY 2020-21 local county budget ask from $17M to $14.3M by deferring the $15/hour classified minimum wage and teacher supplements due to COVID-19 revenue uncertainty, sparking strong pushback from board members who insisted on preserving those commitments and counselor ratios.
disagreements.side_a_position: Restore the $15/hour classified minimum wage, teacher salary supplements, and counselor ratio investments in the county budget request rather than preemptively cutting them.
side_a_arguments: Durham city and county employees already receive $15/hour, and DPS should not ask classified workers or teachers to settle for less.
Removing living-wage and supplement priorities at the start of budget negotiations preemptively concedes core equity commitments before county discussions even begin.
Counselor-to-student ratios and 1:1 device needs remain urgent, especially amid pandemic trauma.
disagreements.side_b_position: Present a trimmed $14.3M baseline request reflecting anticipated COVID-19 economic contractions while keeping deferred items ready to revisit before the May 15 statutory deadline.
side_b_arguments: The MOU budget request is a fluid starting point that can be revised as General Assembly and county revenue impacts become clearer.
Local businesses are shut down and county revenues are expected to contract sharply.
disagreements.resolution: Dr. Mike Lee accommodated the board consensus and the board voted 7-0 to approve an amended $19.38M request restoring the $15/hour minimum wage, teacher supplements, and counselors.

meetings.title: Durham Board of Education Work Session March 12, 2020  5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its March 12, 2020 work session presided over by Work Session Chair Steve Unruhe, the board acted quickly as the COVID-19 crisis escalated, passing the agenda, February 13 minutes, and Hope Valley stormwater easement consent item (7-0), advancing Policy 4000B first reading (7-0), and adopting revised drone Policy 5080/1940 with a second-reading waiver (7-0). Following debate over student absence-note requirements, the board voted 6-1 to waive the attendance requirement of Policy 3410 (high school exam exemptions) during the pandemic (with the single dissenting member not identified by name in the audio transcript). During a pivotal two-hour coronavirus response review—in which Natalie Beyer, Matt Sears, and Minnie Forte-Brown pushed for immediate school closures while Dr. Mike Lee and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga initially favored 2–3 days to organize meals, packets, and employee pay—Dr. Mubenga announced effective Monday, March 16 school closures (`02:22:17`) and the board voted 7-0 to authorize the superintendent to take lawful emergency actions and temporarily waive policies. Following closed session, the board unanimously approved (7-0) the March 12 personnel report and amended the agenda to approve a $403,519 architectural fee increase for Ratio Architects on the Northern High School project (7-0).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Approval, Minutes, and Consent Item
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Work Session Chair Steve Unruhe opened the meeting with a moment of silence and recognized Spanish interpreters. The board unanimously approved (7-0) the agenda, the February 13, 2020 work session minutes, and the single consent item (Hope Valley Elementary stormwater easements).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda passed 7-0; Minutes passed 7-0; Consent passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: Policy 4000B Series First Reading and Drone Policy 5080/1940
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni presented Policy 4000B updates—including systemic racism disproportionality language in Policy 4303, e-cigarettes/vaping in Policy 4320, and removing out-of-school suspension for truancy in Policy 4400—which the board sent to consent for second reading (7-0, excluding held policies). Dr. Julie Pack then presented revised drone Policy 5080/1940 to support Southern High School's FAA Part 107 CTE course, and the board approved it 7-0 while correcting a Wake County typo and waiving second reading.

agenda_items.title: COVID-19 Response Plan, Exam Exemption Waiver (Policy 3410), and School Closure Decision
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga, Dr. Nakia Hardy, Marissa Atkins, Dr. Julius Monk, and Chip Sudderth presented updates on attendance coding, canceling events over 100 people and NCHSAA athletics, suspending facility rentals, employee leave/shared leave pools, and remote learning readiness. The board voted 6-1 to waive Policy 3410's attendance threshold for high school exam exemptions; after intense debate over closure timing, Dr. Mubenga announced DPS schools would close effective Monday, March 16, and the board unanimously (7-0) authorized him to take emergency actions and waive policies in consultation with health officials.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: After unanimously entering closed session (7-0), the board returned to open session at 02:55:48 and unanimously approved (7-0) the March 12, 2020 personnel report. The board then voted 7-0 to amend the open-session agenda and approved a $403,519 fee increase for Ratio Architects on the Northern High School construction project (7-0) before adjourning.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Board of Education Work Session March 12, 2020  5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Parent Note Requirements and Attendance/Exam Policy Waivers During COVID-19 (Policy 3410 6-1 Vote)
disagreements.summary: Board members debated whether requiring parent notes to excuse COVID-related student absences imposed an unnecessary burden during a pandemic, and voted 6-1 to waive Policy 3410's attendance requirement for high school exam exemptions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Eliminate note hurdles and trust families during the pandemic while waiving exam exemption attendance penalties.
side_a_arguments: Requiring parent notes during a global crisis creates unnecessary administrative and family burdens.
Families should be encouraged to keep at-risk children and household members home without truancy letters or exam penalties.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain some form of parent notification (including electronic communication) so data managers can code lawful absences under DPI rules.
side_b_arguments: State DPI attendance statutes govern lawful versus unlawful absence coding.
Schools still need parent notification to account for student whereabouts.
disagreements.resolution: Staff confirmed automated truancy/DA letters would not trigger and electronic notes were acceptable; the board passed the Policy 3410 exam exemption waiver 6-1 (lone dissenter not named in audio).

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Board of Education Work Session March 12, 2020  5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Immediate School Closure vs. Phased Operational Preparation
disagreements.summary: Board members disagreed sharply over whether DPS should close schools immediately on Monday, March 16 for public health protection or take several days to finalize meal distribution, instructional packets, and classified employee pay logistics.
disagreements.side_a_position: Close DPS schools immediately on Monday, March 16 to flatten the curve and protect students, families, and hourly staff.
side_a_arguments: Durham County had severe testing shortages (reportedly only three tests received), meaning community spread was likely already underway.
Proactive school closures ahead of the epidemic curve provide public health protection, whereas reactive closures do not.
Classified staff and families should not remain exposed while neighboring districts like Chapel Hill-Carrboro and Orange were closing.
disagreements.side_b_position: Take 2–3 days to prepare instructional packets, meal distribution, and state legislative guidance on hourly employee pay before closing.
side_b_arguments: Unlike 1:1 districts, DPS lacked devices and internet access for many of its 34,000 students and needed print packets.
Closing without legislative action left hourly classified employees with exhausted leave unpaid and halted school-based breakfast/lunch access.
disagreements.resolution: At 02:22:17, Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga announced DPS would close schools effective Monday, March 16 with detailed guidance issued the next day, and the board voted 7-0 to grant him emergency policy-waiver authority.

meetings.title: Durham Board of Education Emergency Meeting March 11, 2020  6:30
meetings.executive_summary: Chairman Dr. Mike Lee convened an emergency meeting of the Durham Public Schools Board of Education on March 11, 2020 to review the district's coronavirus response plan and grant emergency procurement flexibility. Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga and senior staff outlined CDC-aligned hygiene protocols, phases one and two of the district's pandemic cleaning plan, and immediate cancellation of all student and employee out-of-state travel as well as in-state overnight student field trips (while temporarily retaining small in-district industry/Hub Farm trips). Board members questioned travel criteria, HR leave protections for vulnerable employees, and large event thresholds, and unanimously voted (7-0) to authorize the superintendent to enter into contracts exceeding the $90,000 board threshold without prior approval for COVID-19 emergency response.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chairman Dr. Mike Lee opened the emergency meeting and turned to Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga, who presented CDC-aligned preventative measures, pandemic custodial cleaning phases one and two, and cancellation of out-of-state employee/student travel and overnight field trips. Board members queried staff on keeping small industry field trips open for occupational course of study diploma requirements, large-event restrictions, and HR protections to be detailed at the March 12 work session.

agenda_items.title: Emergency Superintendent Contracting Authorization Above $90,000
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To allow rapid procurement during the emerging COVID-19 response, the board moved, seconded, and unanimously voted (7-0) to authorize the superintendent to enter into contracts above the standard $90,000 board-approval limit without prior board approval specifically for coronavirus emergency response.

meetings.title: Durham Board of Education Monthly Meeting February 27, 2020 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education opened its February 27, 2020 monthly meeting with a moment of silence noting global coronavirus risks, recognized Northern High School Student of the Month Ziki Williams and community mentors, and congratulated Public Affairs staff on three gold awards. During public comment, speakers pressed the board on disproportionate Black male short-term suspensions and restorative practices center referrals, chronic under-resourcing of Exceptional Children services, and mental health equity. The board unanimously approved (7-0) the agenda, January 23 minutes, and a three-item school safety consent agenda (including the NC School Safety Grant contract and Raptor rapid entry system purchase). On a city proposal to establish a Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force, board members reached informal consensus to post the draft bylaws publicly and request five DPS appointments—rather than the three proposed alongside five each for the City and County—while raising questions about staffing funding and School Resource Officer framing before approving the February 27 personnel report (7-0) after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the meeting to order and led a moment of silence highlighting global coronavirus developments. Celebrations honored mentoring groups from the Be Our Guest dinner, Northern High School Student of the Month Ziki Williams, school honorees, and Public Affairs gold award winners, followed by Dr. Pascal Mubenga's superintendent update.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval and January 23, 2020 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved (7-0) the monthly meeting agenda as presented and approved the January 23, 2020 Board of Education meeting minutes by voice vote (7-0).

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Three speakers addressed the board: Millicent Rogers cited Q1 2019 discipline data showing racial disparities in Restorative Practices Center referrals (such as 12% of Black male students vs. 1% of white male students at Riverside); Kelly Cosby criticized systemic underfunding and school-level IEP compliance gaps in Exceptional Children services while praising Dr. Bell; and Ms. Lewis urged equity accountability and announced a free mental health forum at Jordan High School.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: School Safety Grant, Security Contract, and Rapid Entry System
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved (7-0) the consent agenda comprising the North Carolina School Safety Grant contract, the National School Safety and Security Services, Inc. contract, and Raptor/rapid entry system equipment purchases.

agenda_items.title: Board Discussion: Durham Community Safety and Wellness Task Force Bylaws
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members reviewed draft bylaws from Durham City Council members proposing a Community Safety and Wellness Task Force on which DPS would appoint three seats (one education, two youth under 25) versus five seats each for the City and County, with language referencing School Resource Officers and no dedicated administrative funding. Rather than taking a formal vote, the board reached consensus to publish the draft bylaws on the DPS website and request five DPS seats before finalizing participation.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and February 27, 2020 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 7-0 to enter closed session and reconvened at 01:16:40, unanimously approving (7-0) the February 27, 2020 personnel report recommended by Dr. Pascal Mubenga before adjourning.

meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Work Session Chair Xavier Cason (with Dr. Mike Lee arriving late at 02:28:17 after flying from Los Angeles and Matt Sears not recorded in the transcript), the board unanimously approved (5-0) the amended agenda, January 9 minutes, consent items, and a pulled waiver of Policy 4150 Section C allowing displaced McDougald Terrace students to retain seats at Burton and R.N. Harris. The board split 4-1 on aligning all DPS pre-K programs with the Durham Pre-K sliding tuition scale effective July 1, 2020 without granting staff's requested one-year delay for George Watts and Morehead Montessori: Minnie Forte-Brown (mover), Steve Unruhe (seconder), Xavier Cason, and Natalie Beyer voted Aye, while Bettina Umstead voted Nay on grounds of honoring magnet-fair commitments already communicated to Watts and Morehead families. Following closed session and unanimous approval (5-0) of the February 13 personnel report, finance staff Paul LeSieur and Alex Modestou presented the FY 2020-21 budget outlook—detailing state budget delays, $17.8 million in prioritized needs including $15/hour classified wages, EC/EL funding caps, teacher supplements, and $6 million for routine capital maintenance—to visiting local and state candidates and elected officials.

agenda_items.title: Alignment of DPS Pre-K Sliding Tuition Scale with Durham Pre-K

agenda_items.title: Additional Public Comment, Closed Session, and Personnel Report

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Board of Education Work Session February 13, 2020 5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Immediate Universal Pre-K Sliding Scale Alignment at George Watts and Morehead Montessori vs. One-Year Transition Delay
disagreements.summary: The board split 4-1 over whether to apply the Durham Pre-K sliding tuition scale immediately in 2020-21 to George Watts and Morehead Montessori alongside all other DPS Pre-K sites, or grant staff's requested one-year delay to protect families who applied under the older DPS scale.
disagreements.side_a_position: Apply the Durham Pre-K sliding scale uniformly across all DPS Pre-K sites starting July 1, 2020 with no deferment for Watts and Morehead.
side_a_arguments: Durham Pre-K eliminates tuition up to 400% of the federal poverty level, delivering substantial savings to lower- and middle-income families who should not wait another year.
DPS must build one unified universal pre-K system across Durham rather than keeping two scales.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defer implementing the new scale at Watts and Morehead until 2021-22 (or allow families the lesser of the two scales) to honor prior magnet-fair marketing.
side_b_arguments: Families applied to Watts and Morehead in the fall magnet window relying on the published DPS sliding scale, and higher-income families above 400% FPL would face unexpected fee increases.
Consistency and trust require honoring commitments communicated to magnet applicants until the next application cycle.
disagreements.resolution: Minnie Forte-Brown's motion for blanket alignment without a Watts/Morehead deferment passed 4-1, with Bettina Umstead voting Nay and requesting future governance-committee scale changes still appear on DPS agendas for information.

meetings.executive_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee presided over the January 23, 2020 monthly meeting (dated January 24 in archive metadata), opening with celebrations of January Student of the Month, AVID students securing $6 million in college scholarships, and Spark recipients, followed by Dr. Pascal Mubenga's report of 109 winter graduates. The board unanimously approved (7-0) an amended agenda adding a National Mentoring Month proclamation, December 12, 2019 minutes (7-0), the National Mentoring Month proclamation (7-0), and a Career and Technical Education (CTE) Month proclamation (7-0). On operational and capital business, the board unanimously adopted (7-0) the 10-year prioritized capital improvement project list and approved transferring $3,719,538 in 2016 bond funds (7-0) to fund Parkwood Elementary modular classrooms, structural repairs, inoperable boilers, and security vestibules, despite an unnamed board member criticizing $3 million in security vestibule spending as driven by fear rather than data while Chair Lee defended vestibule safety. Finance staff Paul LeSieur and Alex Modestou then presented a comprehensive FY 2020-21 budget outlook—highlighting a $17.7 million request, $7.9 million EC and $3.2 million EL state/federal funding gaps, and private-school tuition comparisons—prompting agreement to brief sitting officials and candidates on February 13, before the board paid tribute to staff supporting McDougald Terrace families and approved the January 23 personnel report (7-0) following closed session.

disagreements.issue: 2016 Bond Funding Allocation for School Security Vestibules
disagreements.summary: During approval of the $3.72 million 2016 bond transfer, a board member criticized spending ~$3 million on security vestibules as driven by fear rather than data, while Chair Dr. Mike Lee defended vestibules as strongly supported by staff, parents, and students.
disagreements.side_a_position: Question allocating roughly $3 million of 2016 bond funds to security vestibules as an over-reaction not grounded in data.
side_a_arguments: Security vestibule spending and active-shooter insurance represent an over-response driven by fear rather than data analysis.
Future capital spending decisions should rely on stronger data analysis.
disagreements.side_b_position: Support completing security vestibule projects as a practical safety enhancement welcomed by school communities.
side_b_arguments: Overwhelmingly, staff, parents, and older students at schools like Rogers-Herr express appreciation for secure front-office entry vestibules.
Vestibules do not disrupt the daily flow of school while providing valuable safety protection.
disagreements.resolution: Despite the recorded policy disagreement, the board approved the full $3,719,538 2016 bond fund transfer 7-0.

meetings.title: Durham Board of Education Work Session January 9, 2020 5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its January 9, 2020 work session, beginning with a moment of silence for McDougall Terrace families and unanimously approving by voice votes an amended agenda and the consent agenda (a contract for Rebound Services). Staff presented an emergency response update on the Durham Housing Authority's temporary relocation of McDougall Terrace residents due to carbon monoxide concerns, detailing bus routing for 107 students across 12 hotels and one private residence using 30 buses, support at Burton Elementary, McKinney-Vento outreach, and nursing health-screening communication. Following discussion of staffing/funding implications and Natalie Beyer's amendment replacing 'minimum' with 'baseline' in the Advanced Academics equity strategy, the board unanimously approved by voice vote an addendum of strategies across eight programmatic areas to the district's strategic plan. The board also received an informational Priority 4 update on family and community engagement (including a Duke Center for Advanced Hindsight enrollment survey, 80% Title I family engagement baseline skepticism, and 92% community partnership coverage) and reached consensus—without a formal vote—to seek a neutral facilitator to convene Durham's 14 brick-and-mortar charter schools rather than immediately sending a local-authorization legislative letter to Raleigh, before entering and returning from closed session with no personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Welcome, Moment of Silence, and Approval of Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee welcomed attendees, introduced DPS ESL teacher Martha Rama-Rigiles as interpreter, and led a moment of silence for children and families affected by the crisis at McDougall Terrace. During agenda review, board members added an update on McDougall Terrace support immediately following the consent agenda and added Natalie Beyer's discussion item on a pilot to improve North Carolina charter school legislation as Item 6C after Item 6B before approving the updated agenda by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment and Consent Agenda (Rebound Services Contract)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee reviewed public comment rules and noted that no speakers had signed up for general public comment. The board then considered the single-item consent agenda—a contract for Rebound Services—and approved it unanimously by voice vote without discussion.
agenda_items.vote_summary: No public speakers; Consent agenda passed unanimously (Voice)

agenda_items.title: McDougall Terrace Relocation Support and Transportation Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Transportation leadership reported that after receiving a Durham Housing Authority student list Sunday afternoon, staff routed 30 buses by Monday morning for displaced McDougall Terrace students—serving 107 students across 8 initial hotels, expanding to 12 hotels and one private residence (adding 572 miles over four days), and noting potential bus/driver and city-county funding constraints if displacement extends beyond the week when year-round schools return from intersession. District staff and board members also recognized Burton Elementary (Dr. Farrell, Travis Anderson, Tina Ingram), McKinney-Vento and student assignment staff, counselors, and Nurse Grady's coordination with school nurses on carbon monoxide exposure information and ongoing screening for families who had not yet evacuated.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: Strategic Plan Addendum Strategies
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Superintendent Dr. Nakia Hardy presented proposed addendum strategies aligned to the existing five strategic plan priorities across eight areas: Advanced Academics (AIG), Career and Technical Education (CTE), ESL/LEP, Multilingual Resource Center, Pre-K, Professional School Counselors, School Boundaries and Student Assignment, and Special Education. Matt Sears raised questions about unbudgeted counselor and CTE Hub Farm staffing implications, while Natalie Beyer questioned voting without deeper staff/task force review and objected to the word 'minimum' in the AIG equity strategy. After Dr. Hardy clarified 'minimum' referred to an equitable baseline of honors/AP/IB courses across all middle and high schools and agreed to update the wording to 'baseline,' the board amended the motion to incorporate Beyer's edit and approved the addendum unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Priority 4 Updates (School, Family, and Community Engagement)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Communications leadership and Goal 4A, 4B, and 4C teams reported mid-year progress on school perception, family participation, and community partnerships, highlighting enrollment growth of over 500 students, Givens/Creekside boundary outreach, multilingual communications led by Pablo Friedman, and a parent enrollment decision-making survey with Duke University's Center for Advanced Hindsight led by Dan Ariely. Board members scrutinized the 80% family engagement baseline derived from Title I schools as overly broad, asked for public inventory and coding of the 92% self-reported community partnerships (noting prior 2016 staffing cuts), and discussed pursuing the adjacent former Durham Visitor Center building for a DPS welcome and multilingual resource center.

agenda_items.title: Item 6C: Pilot to Improve North Carolina Charter School Legislation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Natalie Beyer presented a draft proposal inviting Durham's 14 brick-and-mortar charter schools to explore a local legislative pilot enabling Durham Board of Education authorization/governance—noting 90% of U.S. charter authorizers are LEAs and raising concerns about racial isolation and segregation after state Charter Advisory Board revisions. Board members and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga supported engaging charter leaders locally but cautioned against broadcasting an uncoordinated letter to Raleigh or shifting into unreciprocated operational support like transportation, reaching consensus for administration to identify a neutral facilitator such as the DPS Foundation or a university to convene an initial meeting.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Consensus direction to explore neutral-facilitated local outreach / No vote

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Summary, Closed Session, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk summarized follow-up action items across Items 6A, 6B, and 6C: posting the strategic plan addendum strategies and sharing them with strategic plan partners, inventorying and coding community engagement and partnership supports while updating 2018-19 Teacher Working Conditions data, and identifying a neutral facilitator to invite the 14 charter schools to an initial conversation. The board then voted unanimously by voice vote to enter closed session, returned to open session with no personnel report to approve, and adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed unanimously (Voice); No personnel report

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Board of Education Work Session January 9, 2020 5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Approach to Charter School Local Authorization Pilot and Legislative Outreach
disagreements.summary: Board members disagreed on whether to pursue a formal letter to state education/legislative officials regarding charter school authorization and racial isolation versus focusing strictly on a neutral-facilitated local conversation with Durham's 14 brick-and-mortar charter schools first.
disagreements.side_a_position: Initiate a local-bill authorization pilot conversation and write to the State Board of Education addressing racial isolation and segregation concerns.
side_a_arguments: 90% of charter school authorizers nationwide are local education agencies (LEAs), and local school board governance improves transparency, equity, and accountability.
The NC Charter Advisory Board recently removed language on racial isolation and segregation from its report, warranting a board letter to the State Board.
A local bill in the General Assembly could proceed if even one or two Durham charter schools are interested.
disagreements.side_b_position: Avoid sending an uncoordinated letter to Raleigh or leading with legislation; instead, have a neutral third party convene an initial local listening conversation with Durham charter schools.
side_b_arguments: Sending a broadcast letter to Raleigh without charter school board co-signers or prior organizing would likely be ignored (Dr. Mike Lee).

A legislative bill is far down the road, and charter schools will not engage meaningfully if DPS appears to dictate terms rather than joining a neutral table convened by the DPS Foundation or a university (Steve Unruhe).

Matt Sears questioned the timing and lack of prior charter interest, while Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga cautioned against conversations turning into requests for DPS operational/transportation subsidies without board accountability.
disagreements.resolution: No formal vote was taken; by consensus, the board directed administration to explore a neutral facilitating organization to invite Durham's 14 brick-and-mortar charter schools to an initial local conversation.

meetings.title: Durham Board of Education Monthly Meeting December 12, 2019 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee presided over the December 12, 2019 Durham Public Schools Board of Education monthly meeting with six board members present and Minnie Forte-Brown absent. The board unanimously approved (6-0) all formal action items, including the 2020-21 and 2021-22 traditional and year-round school calendars (incorporating workdays for Yom Kippur and Eid al-Fitr), a $247,000 design-fee change order with Ratio Architects for the Northern High School stadium and athletic facilities, the over-$400 million FY 2019-20 budget resolution alongside a $1.75 million fund balance appropriation ($1 million for Exceptional Children and $750,000 for classified salary study/supplement/custodial obligations), a Clayton/Freeman Street right-of-way consent item, minutes, and the December 12 personnel report. Staff also presented an unmodified, zero-finding FY 2019 CAFR audit noting $26 million in charter school transfers across 46 schools, a McKinney-Vento update documenting over 800 homeless students identified in 2019-20, an update on the K-5 literacy adoption ahead of a January 30 teacher vote, and a preliminary FY 2020-21 budget outlook projecting $17.4 million in baseline requirements plus $4.4 million in deferred needs. No split votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the meeting to order, introduced Spanish interpreter Martha Romo-Eguiles, and led a moment of silence. Celebrations recognized December Student of the Month Ethan Shavinko of Durham Performance Learning Center, longtime Pearsontown Elementary educator Mr. Snipes, and Director of Marketing and Community Engagement Dr. Patricia Hollingsworth with Spark awards.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga highlighted recent school visits including improvements at Parkwood Elementary, urged parents to treat school threats seriously due to manpower and financial costs, and announced local release of classified pay raises and retroactive certified salary supplements before the holidays while awaiting state legislative budget action in January.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval, Minutes Approval, and General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously amended the agenda (6-0) to move the school calendar item to the top of Academic and Operational Services for a family with young children, and approved the November 7 and November 21, 2019 minutes (6-0). During public comment, speakers raised environmental and plumbing/roofing disrepair at Durham School of the Arts and Brian Callaway criticized prior custodial contracting; Chair Lee responded on the record that state review had found Callaway's custodial allegation baseless.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: Clayton/Freeman Street Right-of-Way and Construction Easement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board took up the single consent item approving a right-of-way option purchase and temporary construction easement for the Clayton/Freeman Street project. Following a motion and second with no discussion, the consent agenda passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: 2020-21 and 2021-22 Traditional and Year-Round School Calendars
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Parent Hussein Al-Gank urged formal calendar recognition of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha so Muslim students would not face exam conflicts. Deputy Superintendent Dr. Nakia Hardy presented two-year draft calendars aligning traditional and year-round spring breaks and designating teacher workdays on Yom Kippur and Eid al-Fitr (promising a 2022 addendum shifting the Eid workday placeholder to May 3, 2022); after Steve Unruhe and colleagues discussed parenthesizing religious holidays equitably, the board approved the calendars unanimously.

agenda_items.title: 2019 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) Audit Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief Finance Officer Paul LeSieur and auditor Courtney Wade of Rives & Associates presented the draft FY 2019 CAFR, reporting unmodified opinions on the financial statements and major state/federal programs with zero audit findings, $420 million in total assets, $26 million in total governmental fund balance ($8.4 million unassigned), and $26 million flowing to 46 charter schools serving over 7,000 students. Board members praised the clean audit and urged residents to contact the State Board of Education regarding a proposed 15th Durham charter school in Oak Grove.

agenda_items.title: McKinney-Vento Homeless Education Services Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comment by Carol Mansfield of Families Moving Forward and RTI requesting disaggregated academic outcome tracking, McKinney-Vento Coordinator Ebony Thomas reported serving over 4,800 students since 2014 and over 800 students and siblings thus far in 2019-20 across more than 25 community partners, including a $50,000 BB&T housing grant and the Brogden Middle School resource closet. Board members praised the program, asked for academic outcome disaggregation, and noted shelter concentration should inform upcoming redistricting.

agenda_items.title: Elementary K-5 Literacy Curriculum Adoption Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Executive Director Chanel Sidbury and Dr. Hardy outlined the K-5 literacy RFP vetting three curricula (McGraw-Hill Wonders, HMH Into Reading, and American Reading Company), with teachers voting January 30, 2020 on two core selections and a phased rollout scenario (grades 4-5 first or K-2 first) ahead of a February funding request. Board members pressed on cultural-relevance criteria, phonics versus balanced literacy, and avoiding shelf-sitting materials while preserving autonomy at early-adopter restart schools Glenn and Lakewood.

agenda_items.title: Northern High School Replacement Project Design Fee Change Order
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Facilities staff presented a $247,000 design-fee change order for Ratio Architects to add the stadium, field house, bleachers, press box, concessions, restrooms, and baseball/softball dugouts to the Northern High School replacement contract, bringing the contract total from $2,536,000 to $2,783,000. After confirming the corrected $247,000 figure and welcoming upcoming community fly-through presentations, the board approved the change order unanimously.

agenda_items.title: FY 2019-20 Budget Resolution and $1.75 Million Fund Balance Appropriation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Paul LeSieur presented the over-$400 million FY 2019-20 budget resolution reflecting the ongoing General Assembly budget impasse, $7.25 million in county funding ($1 million below request, requiring $683,000 in DPS operational cuts and $250,000 in lapsed-salary savings), implementation of the classified salary study (1% minimum, 4.4% average raise), and local teacher supplement increases ($5,425 starting). In two consecutive motions, the board unanimously approved the FY 2019-20 budget resolution and a $1.75 million fund balance appropriation ($1 million for Exceptional Children and $750,000 for salary/custodial costs).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Budget resolution passed 6-0; Fund balance appropriation passed 6-0

agenda_items.title: FY 2020-21 Preliminary Budget Planning Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Finance staff outlined preliminary FY 2020-21 budget pressures totaling $17.4 million in core requirements—including $3.8 million in base salary/retirement/utility escalations (state retirement rising from 19.7% to 21.6%), $4.4 million in key priorities ($1.5 million minimum wage, EC, EL support), and $2.24 million for enrollment growth—plus $4.4 million in deferred needs such as $1 million for technology refresh, $1 million for 9 full-time and 37 part-time custodians at $15/hour, and student assignment planning staff. Board members noted DPS maintains 75% of county square footage at $0.28 per square foot versus a $1.67 national average and receives 40% of county debt while facing $727 million in 10-year deferred facility needs.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Approval of December 12, 2019 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session at 03:12:59, reconvened in open session at 03:31:19, and unanimously approved the December 12, 2019 personnel report before adjourning for the holidays.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed 6-0; Personnel report passed 6-0

meetings.executive_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee presided over the November 21, 2019 Durham Public Schools Board of Education monthly meeting with all seven board members present. Following extended debate, the board split 4-3 by voice/hand vote to approve Fall 2020 student reassignment boundaries—adopting the Creekside-to-Parkwood shift as recommended while modifying the Githens/Brogden Middle School line west of US 15-501 to Scenario 1 (NC 751) rather than Cornwallis Road; Steve Unruhe, Matt Sears, and Xavier Cason (per his 01:54:10 clarification) plus one additional supporting member (Natalie Beyer or Bettina Umstead) formed the 4-vote majority, while Dr. Mike Lee, Minnie Forte-Brown, and one additional opposing member (Natalie Beyer or Bettina Umstead) voted Nay (no roll-call names were read on the voice vote). The board voted unanimously (7-0) to transfer $39,611,923 in 2016 bond funds from the New Northern High School ordinance to a new Elementary School C ordinance following county assurances to replenish Northern via LOBs/CIP, replace $989,626 in LOB-ineligible capital projects, adopt a NCSBA resolution demanding the General Assembly remit $729.7 million in unconstitutionally withheld civil penalties (~$15 million owed to DPS), combine December meetings into December 12, and approve consent items (including Policy 6560 second reading), minutes, and the November 21 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened the meeting, introduced Spanish interpreters Martha Genser-Ramirez and Martha Romo-Eguiles, and led a moment of silence. Pearson Elementary Be Our Guest attendees, Hillside student of the month Samia, 2020 Principal of the Year Dr. Jackie Tobias of City of Medicine Academy, NC Eastern Regional Orchestra Teacher of the Year Mr. Walker of Durham School of the Arts, and Spark Pin honorees.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Minutes Approval, and General Public Comment

Harris Elementary for the Durham Tech campus and adopting New Policy 6560 (Disposal of Surplus Property with a $30,000 threshold) on second reading.

agenda_items.title: 2019-2020 Supplemental Capital Improvement Projects Replacement List
agenda_items.discussion_summary: COO Julius Monk reported that county bond counsel determined $989,626 of projects in the board's $6.5 million request—such as playground work—did not qualify for Limited Obligation Bonds (LOBs). disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Board of Education Monthly Meeting November 21, 2019 6:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Githens/Brogden Middle School Boundary West of US 15-501: NC 751 Scenario 1 vs. Cornwallis Road
disagreements.summary: Board members split 4-3 over whether to adopt staff's recommended Cornwallis Road corridor as the southern boundary between Githens and Brogden middle schools or adopt Scenario 1 (NC 751), keeping the Duke Forest/Colony Park pocket in Githens.
disagreements.side_a_position: Adopt Scenario 1 using NC 751 and Duke Forest as the boundary to keep an isolated handful of Forest View/Colony Park students with their neighborhood and elementary cohort.
side_a_arguments: Steve Unruhe argued Scenario 1 only affects a handful of students (~14 across six grades), makes virtually no capacity or operational difference, and keeps the Lemor/Colony Park pocket connected to its surrounding neighborhood.

Matt Sears supported Scenario 1 as consistent with keeping communities connected, and Xavier Cason clarified at 01:54:10 that Duke Forest functions as an undeveloped research-land natural boundary rather than an arbitrary carve-out.
disagreements.side_b_position: Maintain the administration's recommended Cornwallis Road straight-line boundary to avoid setting a precedent of carving out pockets ahead of district-wide redistricting.
side_b_arguments: Dr. Mike Lee emphasized Cornwallis Road is a clean, straight natural corridor and warned against setting a precedent of etching out small residential pockets ahead of full-district redistricting in spring 2020.

Minnie Forte-Brown raised unreadiness during the vote, noting Scenario 1 was feasible rather than staff-recommended and warning that departing from staff's boundary line sets a difficult precedent for larger upcoming redistricting decisions.
disagreements.resolution: Motion adopting Scenario 1 (NC 751) for Githens/Brogden alongside the Creekside/Parkwood recommendation passed 4-3 by voice/hand vote (with one additional Aye and one additional Nay between Natalie Beyer and Bettina Umstead not individually recorded by roll call).

meetings.title: Joint Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Quarterly Meeting  November 12, 2019 9:00
meetings.executive_summary: Board of Education Chair Dr. Mike Lee and Board of County Commissioners Chair Wendy Jacobs co-convened the November 12, 2019 joint quarterly meeting, with BOE members Dr. Mike Lee, Bettina Umstead, Xavier Cason, Steve Unruhe, and Minnie Forte-Brown (arriving after opening remarks) confirmed participating. Both boards unanimously approved the agenda and September 17, 2019 joint minutes by voice vote. During the centerpiece capital discussion, county financial advisor Doug Carter and Budget Director Keith Lane warned that DPS's $816 million in 10-year capital needs (and $254 million single-year peak) would push the county's CIP to $1.36 billion ($3,800 per capita) and strain AAA credit metrics and project-management capacity, whereas DPS board members pressed for firm funding assurances before spending $51 million in 2016 bond funds. Both boards reached informal consensus—declining a formal roll-call vote on Steve Unruhe's proposed motion—to proceed immediately with Elementary School C using existing 2016 bond funds, replenish Northern High School via Limited Obligation Bonds (LOBs) and the CIP, and revisit Elementary School F, deferred maintenance, and broader CIP prioritization at the January work session, followed by a brief Durham Pre-K governance update.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Agenda Approval, and September 17, 2019 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the joint BOE-BOCC meeting to order and led a moment of silence. Both boards unanimously approved the agenda and the September 17, 2019 joint meeting minutes by voice votes, with appreciation noted for the detailed minutes.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda passed unanimously (Joint); Minutes passed unanimously (Joint)

agenda_items.title: Options for Funding Elementary Schools C and F and County CIP Capacity
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County financial advisor Doug Carter and Budget Director Keith Lane presented Durham County's AAA credit constraints, noting DPS represents 42% of outstanding county debt, the 2007 bond ($195 million) took 11 years to spend, and adding all DPS facility-assessment needs ($816 million over 10 years, including DSA upgrades and Elementary F) would push the CIP to $1.36 billion ($3,800 per capita). BOE members (Dr. Mike Lee, Steve Unruhe, Bettina Umstead, Minnie Forte-Brown, Xavier Cason) and commissioners reached informal consensus—rather than taking a formal floor vote on Steve Unruhe's motion—to launch Elementary School C using 2016 GO bond funds, commit to funding Northern High School through LOBs/CIP, and prioritize Elementary School F and deferred needs in January ahead of a potential 2022 bond referendum.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informal joint consensus reached (no formal vote taken)

agenda_items.title: Update on Durham Pre-K
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Michelle Pell and Mr. Cummings presented an update on Durham Pre-K expansion and the newly launched website (durhamprek.org). In response to board questions, staff confirmed Dr. Hardy represents DPS on the Durham Pre-K Governance Committee chaired by Dr. Iheoma Iruka with Dr. Wakisha Glass of NCCU as vice chair before Chair Lee adjourned the meeting at 01:54:51.
