disagreements.meeting_title: Joint Board of Education and Board of County Commissioners Quarterly Meeting  November 12, 2019 9:00
disagreements.issue: Capital Spending Pace, 2020 vs. 2022 Bond Timing, and Funding Commitments for Northern HS, Elementary C, and Elementary F
disagreements.summary: School board members and county officials/commissioners clashed over why 2016 Northern High School bond funds remained unspent, whether DPS could absorb $400 million in short-term capital spending without jeopardizing Durham County's AAA bond rating, and how to balance Elementary School F and deferred school maintenance against county CIP priorities.
disagreements.side_a_position: DPS needs an explicit county funding commitment to replenish Northern High School (via LOBs) before spending 2016 bond money on Elementary School C, plus urgent action on Elementary School F and deferred maintenance.
side_a_arguments: Dr. Mike Lee and Steve Unruhe explained DPS had held the $51 million in 2016 bonds because touching Northern High School funds without a formal county replacement commitment would alarm Northern families.

Bettina Umstead and Minnie Forte-Brown urged the county to bring prioritized CIP trade-offs to the January meeting and act on critical red/yellow facility needs rather than delaying construction while costs escalate.
disagreements.side_b_position: Durham County must preserve AAA credit metrics, manage per-capita CIP load ($1.36B), align the next GO bond to 2022, and constrain near-term spending to realistic project-management capacity.
side_b_arguments: County financial advisor Doug Carter and Budget Director Keith Lane noted DPS averaged $19–20 million/year historically (taking 11 years to spend $195 million from 2007) and warned rating agencies would scrutinize a proposed $254 million single-year peak.

County staff and BOCC Chair Wendy Jacobs emphasized all county departments, EMS, libraries, and youth detention compete from the same funding pot and urged DPS to submit prioritized needs ahead of a 2022 bond referendum.
disagreements.resolution: Resolved by informal joint consensus (declining a formal floor vote on Steve Unruhe's motion) to proceed with Elementary School C using 2016 bond funds, replenish Northern High School via LOBs and the CIP, and revisit Elementary School F and broader CIP prioritization at the January work session.

meetings.title: Durham Board of Education Work Session September 12 , 2019    5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: With all seven board members present and Minnie Forte-Brown presiding (all other six members moved, seconded, or took points of privilege under the chair), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its September 12, 2019 work session (video dated 2019-09-13). The board unanimously approved (7-0) two major capital actions: authorizing the board chair and superintendent to purchase two parcels (19 acres for $716,690 and 57 acres for $2,565,000, totaling $553,000 below appraised value) for the new Northern High School targeted to open in August 2023, and authorizing staff to request Durham County increase its unbudgeted Limited Obligation Bond capital appropriation from $3.655 million to $6.55 million to address urgent HVAC and deferred maintenance across 47-year-old school buildings. The board also unanimously approved (7-0) the agenda, August 8 minutes, closed session, and the September 12 personnel report, while receiving briefings on FY 2018-19 academic accountability gains and a Capacity Optimization Analysis projecting K-3 class-size non-compliance and 820 needed classrooms by 2021-22.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Agenda Approval, and August 8, 2019 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The presiding chair called the work session to order, led a moment of silence, and presided over unanimous 7-0 voice votes approving the agenda (moved by Natalie Beyer, seconded by Steve Unruhe) and the August 8, 2019 work session minutes (moved by Steve Unruhe, seconded by Bettina Umstead).

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment and Insurance Coverages Briefing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Brian Callaway urged filling the energy/sustainability coordinator role and criticized executive raises while classified staff lagged behind the city/county $15/hour wage. Staff then briefed the board on annual insurance premiums—adding $3,000 for active-shooter coverage and committing to bid coverages next spring—and paused for a parent requesting expanded autism programming near Little River Elementary.

agenda_items.title: 2018-2019 Accountability Results and Strategic Plan Year 1 Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julie Spencer and Dr. Nakia Hardy reported meeting Year 1 strategic plan targets with gains in school performance grades (including Lakewood Middle, Rogers-Herr, and Watts rising from C to B), EVAAS growth, science proficiency, and graduation rate, while flagging Math 3 proficiency (85.1% for the cohort), English learner progress (WIDA ACCESS), and an ACT score bubble at 15–16. Staff also highlighted the Southern High School Skilled Trades Academy and Zello career-planning platform.

agenda_items.title: Secondary Public Comment and Point of Privilege (NCSBA District 3 Meeting)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speaker Mr. Jones urged DPS to connect Southern High School skilled trades graduates to upcoming downtown bond construction jobs and encouraged a bold $95M–$160M school bond ask. On a point of privilege, Board Chair Dr. Mike Lee thanked Lucas Middle School, Northern culinary students, Rogers-Herr art students, Hillside, Riverside, DSA, Southern's drum line, and DPS administrative assistants for hosting the well-received NCSBA District 3 meeting.

agenda_items.title: Authorization to Purchase Land for New Northern High School
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a completed 120-day due diligence period covering environmental, subsurface, title, ALTA survey, and appraisals, staff recommended purchasing a 19-acre parcel for $716,690 ($283,310 under appraisal) and a 57-acre parcel for $2,565,000 ($135,000 under appraisal) toward a new Northern High School targeted to open in August 2023. Moved by Steve Unruhe and seconded by Xavier Cason, the board authorized the chair and superintendent to execute purchase agreements unanimously (7-0) while urging community outreach in Northern, Lucas, and Carrington.

agenda_items.title: Capacity Optimization Analysis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Strategic Planning Director W. Matthew Palmer presented a district-wide Capacity Optimization Analysis stemming from the May 2019 joint BOCC meeting, projecting that without adjustments DPS will be non-compliant with state K-3 class-size caps in grades 1–3 by 2021-22 (requiring 820 elementary classrooms), alongside overutilization at seven elementary schools while protecting 56 pre-kindergarten classrooms.

agenda_items.title: Unbudgeted County Appropriation Request for Capital and Deferred Maintenance ($6.55 Million)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Travis Anderson and Thomas Griffith reported that DPS schools average 47 years in age and had already incurred over $500,000 in emergency repairs three weeks into the school year due to deferred HVAC, gas-line, and water-main failures. Moved by Xavier Cason and seconded by Matt Sears and Natalie Beyer, the board unanimously (7-0) approved requesting Durham County increase its unbudgeted capital appropriation from $3.655 million to $6.55 million alongside the miscellaneous capital improvements list.

agenda_items.title: Summary of Follow-Up Items, Closed Session, and September 12, 2019 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff recapped follow-up items for the upcoming joint county meeting, Dr. Lee thanked Dr. Pittman and Jeremy Tucker, and the board voted 7-0 (moved by Dr. Mike Lee, seconded by Bettina Umstead) to enter closed session, reconvening at 03:15:26 to unanimously approve the September 12, 2019 personnel report.

meetings.title: Durham Board of Education Work Session August 8 , 2019 5:00
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 8, 2019 work session (dated August 9 in the video metadata), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education opened with a moment of silence for victims of the Dayton and El Paso mass shootings and the 680 families affected by ICE workplace arrests in Mississippi, and heard public comment from parent Paul Edick King requesting district-wide busing for out-of-district New Tech High School students comparable to Hillside High School's IB program. The board unanimously approved its agenda, the June 6, 2019 minutes, and a consent contract for 2019-2020 DPS vision services. Following a detailed presentation by Dr. Debbie Pittman on lottery priority filters and Exceptional Children (EC) separate-setting placements, the board unanimously adopted an administration-drafted sibling preference policy unifying families with students in EC separate settings and requested follow-up on transfer policies, magnet capacity, and family outreach. The board also unanimously endorsed a resolution/letter welcoming refugees and immigrants (welcomingrefugees2020.org) brought forward by Chair Dr. Mike Lee and unanimously approved the August 8, 2019 personnel report after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Interpreter Introductions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The work session was called to order for August 8, 2019, and the board observed a moment of silence and prayer for victims of the Dayton, Ohio and El Paso, Texas shootings as well as 680 families impacted by ICE arrests in Mississippi. Spanish interpreters Ms. Flowers (community liaison and Riverside High School alumna) and Martha Romer-Rugalis (DPS ESL teacher) were introduced, and Vice Chair Bettina Umstead joined at 00:04:28.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the work session agenda as written. A motion and second were made, and the agenda passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment: New Tech High School Bus Transportation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Paul Edick King, parent of a ninth-grade student at New Tech High School on the Hillside High School campus, spoke on behalf of families with out-of-district students. He argued that because Hillside's IB program provides district-wide bus transportation for out-of-district students, the same transportation resources should automatically extend to New Tech High School students on the same campus.

agenda_items.title: Approval of June 6, 2019 Board Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the minutes from the June 6, 2019 meeting. A motion and second were made and approved unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: 2019-2020 DPS Vision Services Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered the single consent item, the DPS vision services contract for the 2019-2020 school year. After a motion and second, the contract was approved unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Sibling Preference Policy for Students with Disabilities (EC Separate Settings)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Hardy and Dr. Debbie Pittman (Assistant Superintendent of Specialized Services) presented on magnet/year-round lottery priority filters and the lack of sibling preference for students placed in Exceptional Children (EC) separate-setting classrooms. Board members criticized the complexity of existing lottery rules for families, emphasized person-first language ('students with disabilities'), connected the change to broader transfer policy and magnet evaluation work, and unanimously adopted the written sibling preference policy.

agenda_items.title: Board Chair Item: Resolution/Letter Welcoming Refugees
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee presented a letter from welcomingrefugees2020.org inviting elected officials to reaffirm community support for resettling refugees and immigrants. Board members voiced strong support in light of recent national events, unanimously voted to endorse the letter, and directed staff to post it as a signed board resolution on the website while members also signed individually online.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items, Closed Session, and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff summarized three follow-up items resulting from the sibling preference vote: reviewing transfer policy, checking magnet school capacity numbers, and communicating with affected families and school leaders. The board unanimously entered closed session at 01:04:36, reconvened at 02:54:23, and unanimously approved the August 8, 2019 personnel report presented by Dr. Pascal Mubenga before adjourning.

meetings.title: Board of Education Retreat Saturday, July 20, 2019 at 8:30 PM – 3:00 PM Session 1
meetings.executive_summary: In Session 1 of its July 20, 2019 Organizational Meeting and Retreat, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously re-elected Dr. Mike Lee as Board Chair (6-0) and Bettina Umstead as Vice Chair (6-0) under Policy 2200. The board unanimously amended its retreat agenda to remove Item 8 (sibling preference, deferred to the August work session at Steve Unruhe's request) and unanimously approved shifting future work session start times from 4:30 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. to better accommodate working board members and high school dismissal. Administration and board members then held a lengthy policy dialogue on expanding universal pre-K amidst federal Title I funding caps and the unfunded state K-3 class size mandate, noting the interdependence between pre-K space and redistricting. The morning session concluded with a facilitated gallery walk workshop on magnet programs, equity, and diversity led by Ms. Marion.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Welcome, and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mike Lee called the Organizational Meeting and Retreat to order, stated the purposes of electing the Board Chair and Vice Chair and conducting retreat planning business, noted the webcast, and led a moment of silence.

agenda_items.title: Organizational Elections: Board Chair and Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga presided over the chair election under Policy 2200; Dr. Mike Lee was the sole nominee and was elected unanimously with all six members present voting aye. Chair Lee then conducted the Vice Chair election, where Bettina Umstead was unanimously elected; both leaders gave brief remarks emphasizing student equity and making DPS Exceptional Children services the best in the nation.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Chair Lee passed 6-0; Vice Chair Umstead passed 6-0

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Amendments
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board added Item 4B to discuss the work session calendar and, at Steve Unruhe's request, removed Item 8 (sibling preference) so the retreat could remain focused on annual planning and sibling preference could be addressed at the August work session. meetings.title: Board of Education Retreat Saturday, July 20, 2019 at 8:30 PM – 3:00 PM Session 2
meetings.executive_summary: Session 2 of the July 20, 2019 Board of Education Retreat was a non-voting strategic discussion continuing the board's review of magnet programs, equity, and student assignment prior to lunch. Board members and facilitator Ms. Marion examined Dr. Bullock's draft universal definition of equity, classroom-level diversity gaps (such as AP courses), and stark supply-and-demand imbalances in the magnet lottery—including ~9,000 elementary applications (~2,580 unique applicants) competing for 705 seats. Members raised equity concerns about George Watts Montessori (where sibling preference and walk-zone priorities left few or no general seats for Black and brown students), Durham School of the Arts (DSA), magnets operating 'in name only,' and inconsistent shuttle-versus-countywide bus transportation. To guide staff and planner Matthew Palmer's upcoming review, board members articulated key principles including reducing application and transportation complexity, auditing extra funding per magnet school, strengthening neighborhood schools, grandfathering current students, and evaluating magnets school-by-school to avoid unintended consequences.

agenda_items.title: Debrief of Magnet Gallery Walk and Draft Universal Equity Definition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members and Ms. Marion debriefed their strengths-and-challenges gallery walk, noting perceptions that some magnet programs feel exclusive or unwelcoming and highlighting how magnet seat caps differ from uncapped neighborhood attendance zones. Ms. Marion also reviewed Dr. Bullock's draft universal equity definition—incorporating students with disabilities and MTSS differentiation—and noted that school-wide diversity does not always translate to classroom-level equity in AP classes.

agenda_items.title: Magnet Lottery Demand, Sibling/Walk-Zone Priorities, and Transportation Equity
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Ms. Marion walked the board through elementary, middle, and high school magnet lottery application data (e.g., Burton receiving 322 applications for 41 seats, and ~9,000 total elementary choices from ~2,580 applicants for 705 seats reduced further by K-3 class size limits). Board members questioned the value of third-choice rankings, raised alarms over gentrification, sibling preference, and walk zones crowding Black and brown applicants out of George Watts Montessori pre-K and DSA, and flagged complex disparities between shuttle stops and county-wide busing.

agenda_items.title: Board Guiding Principles for Magnet Program Evaluation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members gave staff and planner Matthew Palmer guiding principles to follow up on the 2016 magnet study: Steve Unruhe called for reducing application and transportation complexity, scrutinizing resource equity between magnet and traditional schools, evaluating school-by-school (supporting distinct models like City of Medicine), and humility regarding unintended consequences. Other members emphasized grandfathering current student trajectories, strengthening neighborhood schools, simplifying onboarding, and obtaining race/SES applicant-versus-enrollment breakdowns and per-school magnet financial data before adjourning for lunch.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Board of Education Work Session June 6, 2019 4:30
disagreements.issue: School-level opt-outs vs. universal implementation of K-5 Eureka Math curriculum
disagreements.summary: Following public comment from Club Boulevard Elementary parents requesting an opt-out or slower transition from Bridges Math, board members differed over whether to formalize school-level implementation flexibility or enforce uniform district-wide adoption to close racial achievement gaps. Ultimately, the board approved the Great Minds Eureka Math contract unanimously (5-0) while leaving school-level pacing as an administrative responsibility rather than adopting a board policy opt-out.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support gradual, differentiated rollout flexibility for schools with existing math curricula
side_a_arguments: Respect the professional judgment and prior investments of principals and teachers at schools already using vetted curricula like Bridges Math
Provide differentiated professional development and avoid overwhelming teachers and families with rapid simultaneous math and ELA changes
Treat school-level implementation pacing as tactical administrative discretion rather than a rigid top-down mandate
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose formal school opt-outs or citywide flexibility that leaves vulnerable students behind
side_b_arguments: All 30 elementary schools participated in the vote (19-11 for Eureka Math), making the selection participatory rather than top-down

Stark 3rd-grade math proficiency gaps persist (48.6% for Black males and 49.8% for Black females vs. ~85% for white students), and mobile low-income students suffer when transferring between schools with mismatched curricula
A slower rollout is acceptable only if every school commits to implementing Eureka Math rather than opting out

meetings.executive_summary: At its May 22, 2019 monthly meeting, Board Chair Dr. Mike Lee and the Durham Public Schools Board of Education devoted the opening hour to extensive end-of-year student, teacher, transportation, and school recognitions, followed by a brief Superintendent's Update from Dr. Pascal Mubenga and unanimous (7-0) approvals of the agenda and April 25, 2019 minutes. agenda_items.title: Long-Range Facility Assessment Plan Presentation (Cumming Corporation)

meetings.title: Durham Board of Education Work Session May 9, 2019 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its May 9, 2019 work session (presided over by Vice Chair Bettina Umstead as 'Madam Chair'), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved an amended agenda, the April 11 minutes, and consent items reallocating athletic/tennis-court lighting funds. The board unanimously approved StudySync (McGraw-Hill Education) as the secondary literacy core curriculum alongside its contract (moved by Matt Sears, seconded by Minnie Forte-Brown), while urging administration and the Office of Equity Affairs to build a bank of culturally relevant supplemental materials. Following a Strategic Plan Priority 5 update highlighting clean 2017-18 audits, custodial insourcing, K-3 space planning, security vestibules (where Matt Sears criticized vestibule spending over counselors while Steve Unruhe defended operations staff and urged enhancing physical learning environments), and $2.4 million in local transportation costs, the board unanimously approved a five-year Edmentum e-learning contract saving $478,350 and a $316,000 Category 2 E-Rate contract with Tiber Creek Consulting ($63,000 district share after an 80% federal discount). The board also unanimously advanced first readings of Policies 3410 and 3430 (making students voting members of school improvement teams), adopted the 2019-2020 board calendar—including holding the July 20 organizational meeting at the retreat and scheduling a May 30 long-range facilities meeting—and approved the May 9, 2019 personnel report after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Amended Agenda, Minutes, Consent, and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Bettina Umstead opened the meeting, introduced Spanish interpreter Martha Ramirez, and led a moment of silence for recent North Carolina and national shooting victims. The board unanimously approved the amended agenda (adding the board calendar at 8C, moved by Natalie Beyer, seconded by Matt Sears), the April 11 minutes, consent athletic-upgrade bids, and heard early public comment from Bill Garrity; later at 00:59:01, Rebound director Amy Reubline sought advocacy for state House legislative grant renewal and Latino Padres mothers thanked teachers after attending the May 1 Raleigh rally.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Amended agenda passed 7-0; Minutes passed 7-0; Consent passed 7-0

agenda_items.title: Secondary Literacy Curriculum Adoption (StudySync / McGraw-Hill Education)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nikia Hardy and Chanel Sidbury presented the RFP and site-based voting process (where StudySync won 15 first-choice and 10 second-choice votes over MyPerspectives and American Reading Company, funded via ~$2.3M in textbook allotment) alongside an equity review by Jermaine Porter. Board members (Matt Sears moving, Minnie Forte-Brown seconding) unanimously adopted StudySync and its McGraw-Hill contract subject to legal data-privacy edits, while urging central staff to compile culturally relevant supplemental texts.

agenda_items.title: Strategic Plan Priority 5 Update: Fiscal and Operational Responsibility
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julie Spencer updated the board on Priority 5 benchmarks: a clean 2017-18 audit and ASBO financial award, in-house custodial baselines under Ralph France, K-3 1:19 class-size planning with ORed, security vestibules (26 complete, 25 planned), and transportation efficiency ($2.4M local funding). Matt Sears criticized security vestibule spending as creating 'prison-like' entrances at the expense of counselors, while Steve Unruhe pushed back on Sears's broader critique of operations, concurred on tracking learning-environment upgrades, and Minnie Forte-Brown urged aligning DPS with the County Commissioners' $15/hour minimum wage push.

agenda_items.title: E-Learning Platform RFP and Five-Year Edmentum Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chanel Sidbury and Digital Teaching & Learning Director Ron Wayland recommended renewing Edmentum for five years following an RFP vetted by >100 students, assistive technology staff, and ESL co-teaching reviewers. The contract locks in rates saving $478,350 over five years, drops unused CTE prep coursework to save $100,000 annually, and passed unanimously subject to legal negotiations, with a request for follow-up data on NCVPS and NCSSM online courses.

agenda_items.title: E-Rate Category 2 Managed Broadband Contract (Tiber Creek Consulting)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief Technology Officer Dr. Candice Hosey updated the board on Category 1 internet access (Spectrum/Charter contract expiring after 2019-20) and requested approval of a $316,000 Category 2 Managed Internal Broadband Services (MBIS) award to lowest-bidder Tiber Creek Consulting for daily onsite network support. With an 80% federal E-Rate discount ($252,000), DPS's net cost is ~$63,000; the board approved the Category 2 application/contract unanimously and requested the full five-bidder list.

agenda_items.title: Policy First Readings (Policies 3410, 3430, and Textbook Selection)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented policy updates clarifying that EOC exams account for 20% of course grades (Policy 3410) and adding middle and high school students to School Improvement Teams (Policy 3430). Following board feedback to make student representatives voting rather than non-voting members, the board unanimously accepted first reading and advanced the policies to the regular meeting consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: 2019-2020 Board Calendar, Organizational Meeting, and Redistricting Meetings
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members set the annual Organizational Meeting for the July 20 retreat, agreed by consensus to hold a special May 30 meeting at 5:30 p.m. to receive the Long-Range Facility Plan, supported scheduling dedicated community-accessible redistricting meetings during 2019-2020, corrected Good Friday to April 10, and unanimously adopted the 2019-2020 board calendar updates.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and May 9, 2019 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After summarizing follow-up items and Umstead noting she spoke earlier that day honoring Mickey Michaux at Hayti Heritage Center, the board unanimously entered closed session at 02:55:01, reconvened at 04:12:44, and unanimously approved the May 9, 2019 personnel report before adjourning.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session April 11, 2019 4:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Chaired by Dr. Mike Lee, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education approved its amended afternoon work session agenda—pulling Consent Items A and B for discussion—and adopted the March 14, 2019 minutes with Natalie Beyer's clarification on Spanish-speaking mental health services. The sole split vote of the meeting came on Consent Item A, changing bell schedules for Y.E. Smith and C.C. Spaulding Elementary Schools to an 8:30 a.m. start and ending extended day: moved by Steve Unruhe and seconded by Bettina Umstead, with Minnie Forte-Brown backing teacher votes of 99% and 77%, Natalie Beyer questioning premature abandonment of extended day and start-time equity, and Dr. Mike Lee warning against setting a precedent of school-chosen bell times while not delaying the vote, the motion passed 5-1 by voice vote with one board member absent and the lone Nay voter not identified by name on the audio record. The board unanimously approved Consent Item B (Participate Learning Dual Language purchase agreements totaling $113,000 plus a $30,000 performance guarantee for Bethesda, Lakewood, and Southwest Elementary Schools), Consent Items C through G, a resolution supporting the May 1 Day of Action for NC Public Schools, and Dr. Patricia Ashley's reappointment to the Durham Tech Board of Trustees. HR and Finance staff also presented Phase 2 of the Classified and Administrator Salary Study covering roughly 700 employees in grades 57-78 contingent on $1.5 million in requested county funding.

Spaulding) to move to an 8:30 a.m. start and end extended day while retaining after-school tutoring and fitting within existing bus tiers. agenda_items.title: Consent Item B (Pulled): Participate Learning Academic Services Purchase Agreements

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session April 11, 2019 4:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Bell Schedule Change and Ending Extended Day at Y.E. Smith and C.C. Spaulding Elementary Schools
disagreements.summary: Board members divided 5-1 on a staff-requested change moving Y.E. Smith and C.C. Spaulding Elementary Schools to an 8:30 a.m. start time and ending their extended school day, debating whether halting extended-day turnaround programming and granting two schools an 8:30 a.m. start set an inequitable districtwide precedent.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the 8:30 a.m. bell schedule change in deference to strong school staff support while retaining after-school intervention options.
side_a_arguments: School faculty overwhelmingly backed the change (99% at Y.E. Smith and 77% at C.C. Spaulding) and principals committed to keeping after-school tutoring and enrichment.
Transportation confirmed the 8:30 a.m. schedule fits existing bus tiers without harming fleet efficiency, and extended day had not demonstrated the intended academic gains.
disagreements.side_b_position: Question ending extended-day turnaround programming before full evaluation and oppose setting a precedent of individual schools choosing 8:30 a.m. start times.
side_b_arguments: Shortening the instructional day walks back a deliberate turnaround strategy for struggling schools without clear long-term evaluation.
Because bus tiering forced many elementary schools into much earlier start times during the systemwide bell-time flip, granting two schools 8:30 a.m. starts raises fairness and precedent concerns.
disagreements.resolution: Passed 5-1 on a voice vote with one board member absent and the lone Nay voter unnamed in the audio record (Steve Unruhe moved, Bettina Umstead seconded; Natalie Beyer raised evaluation/equity questions and Dr. Mike Lee cautioned against setting a school-chosen start-time precedent while stating the board would not delay the request).

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting March 21
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee with Matt Sears absent, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education acted on a wide slate of instructional, budgetary, and policy items during its March 2019 monthly meeting. The board voted 6-0 to amend its agenda, adopt the February 28, 2019 minutes, authorize Dual Language Immersion expansion planning at Bethesda, Lakewood, and Southwest Elementary Schools (after board questions on demographic equity, magnet access, and middle-school feeder pathways), adopt Section 1000 Board Policies on second reading, pledge up to $24,000 contingent funding for a Community Kitchen Feasibility Study, and endorse a City of Durham Safe Routes to School grant letter. On the Superintendent's Proposed FY 2019-20 Budget, members voted 6-0 to amend the county capital outlay request upward from $1 million to $6 million and approved the $12.8 million new local funding ask ($8.2 million operating plus $4.6 million added capital) 6-0. The sole contested vote was a 5-1 voice approval authorizing Take Two summer EOG/EOC retesting (~$250,000 in state/federal funds for ELA and science): while one unnamed member opposed spending $250,000 on high-stakes 'bubble test' culture, another supporter defended retesting to prepare students for standardized exams like the ACT, LSAT, and MCAT and Deputy Superintendent Dr. Nakia Hardy noted NCDPI requires annual authorization for the earmarked funds; because it was an unrecorded voice vote with Matt Sears noted absent, the lone Nay voter among the six present members (Dr. Mike Lee, Bettina Umstead, Natalie Beyer, Minnie Forte-Brown, Xavier Cason, Steve Unruhe) was not individually named on the audio record. Following closed session, the board approved the March 21 personnel report 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Celebrations, Amended Agenda, and February 28 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the meeting to order, held a moment of silence, and recognized district student and staff honorees including spelling bee winners and CTE achievements. With Matt Sears absent, the board voted 6-0 to amend the agenda to add a Safe Routes to School support letter and approved the February 28, 2019 minutes 6-0.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public commenters included substitute teacher Bill Garrity (seeking sub recognition and raises), Durham Association of Educators member Xavier Adams (requesting district advocacy on state legislative pay and per-pupil cuts), and Durham County Commissioner Brenda Howerton / community speakers advocating for the Community Kitchen Feasibility Study.

agenda_items.title: Dual Language Immersion Expansion Planning
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Academic Services staff requested authorization to plan Dual Language Immersion kindergarten cohorts at Bethesda and Lakewood Elementary Schools alongside ongoing expansion at Southwest Elementary, with ~$120,000 in Participate Learning service agreements to follow in April. Board members pressed staff on Black student representation, neighborhood versus magnet access, Northern Durham coverage, and middle-school continuity before voting 6-0 to proceed with planning.

agenda_items.title: Summer Learning Update and Take Two EOG/EOC Retesting Authorization
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and Jamie Stroud reviewed 2019 summer programs—Operation Literacy, Read to Achieve camps, ESL Newcomer Academy, Extended School Year, Spark AIG, and High School Credit Options—and sought annual NCDPI-required authorization for Take Two EOG/EOC retesting (~$250,000 in state/federal funds, limited to ELA and science due to state math renorming). After debate over high-stakes testing versus alternative instructional uses, the authorization passed 5-1 by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Proposed FY 2019-20 Budget
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Paul LeSieur presented the Superintendent's Proposed FY 2019-20 Budget requesting $8.2 million in new county operating funds (covering $4,900-to-$5,425 certified supplement raises, $2.6 million for strategic plan positions moved off fund balance, $1.5 million for Phase 2 classified salary adjustments, and $500,000 for full-time custodians) plus $1 million in new capital outlay. Board members unanimously amended the capital request upward from $1 million to $6 million (+$4.6 million new funds) and adopted the $12.8 million county ask 6-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Capital amendment passed 6-0; Budget passed 6-0 as amended (Voice)

agenda_items.title: Board Policy Manual Transition: Section 1000 Adoption (Second Reading)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni presented Section 1000 Board Policies for second-reading adoption, incorporating board equity edits in Policy 1100 and 'family and guardian' terminology updates while excluding Policy 1750 pending legal review. The board adopted Section 1000 unanimously 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Community Kitchen Feasibility Study Support
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Operational Services and Child Nutrition leadership discussed partnering with Durham County, City of Durham, and food security partners on a $120,000 Community Kitchen Feasibility Study. The board voted 6-0 to commit up to $24,000 contingent on the remaining funding being secured from partner organizations.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Added during agenda review, staff and board members reviewed a City of Durham Safe Routes to School grant application supporting pedestrian and bicycle safety improvements near DPS campuses. The board unanimously approved sending the letter of support 6-0.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 6-0 to enter closed session for personnel and confidential legal matters. Reconvening in open session, the board approved the March 21, 2019 personnel report 6-0 before adjourning.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting March 21
disagreements.issue: Take Two Summer EOG/EOC Retesting Authorization ($250,000 Earmarked State/Federal Funds)
disagreements.summary: The board split 5-1 on authorizing Take Two summer EOG/EOC retesting (~$250,000, limited to ELA and science in 2019 because state math tests were being renormed), contrasting skepticism of high-stakes standardized testing with arguments for student proficiency opportunities and future exam readiness.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve Take Two summer retesting using earmarked state and federal funds and comply with annual NCDPI authorization requirements.
side_a_arguments: Earmarked state and federal funds were budgeted specifically for retesting and cannot simply be diverted outside testing requirements.
Retesting builds student confidence and prepares students for future gatekeeper standardized exams such as the ACT, LSAT, MCAT, and bar exam.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose spending $250,000 on additional high-stakes 'bubble tests' when North Carolina promotion decisions do not require retesting.
side_b_arguments: High-stakes standardized 'bubble testing' creates misplaced incentives to boost scores rather than investing the $250,000 in more meaningful summer instruction.
Principals retain promotion discretion under state law without relying on summer retests.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session February 7, 2019 4:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Aligning 2019-20 Traditional and Year-Round Spring Breaks Over Year-Round School Preferences
disagreements.summary: Following the board's January 24 referral of spring break dates back to schools, members clashed over whether to enforce a single districtwide spring break (Draft B) or honor the 4-1 (80%) vote by year-round schools to retain Draft A.
disagreements.side_a_position: Align traditional and year-round spring break weeks districtwide to simplify scheduling for multi-school families.
side_a_arguments: 61% of all voting DPS schools preferred having a single common spring break across traditional and year-round calendars, and 73% of overall school votes backed Draft B.
Families with children attending both traditional and year-round campuses face childcare and vacation disruptions when spring breaks fall in different weeks.
disagreements.side_b_position: Respect the 80% (4-1) vote of year-round schools favoring Draft A and avoid forcing Draft B's mid-quarter disruption onto year-round calendars.
side_b_arguments: Four of five year-round schools repeatedly voted for Draft A because Draft B cuts two weeks into their third-quarter instructional cycle right before intercession.
Overriding a 4-1 campus majority among year-round schools contradicts the district's collaborative calendar-voting process.
disagreements.resolution: When Chair Dr. Mike Lee called at 01:31:51 for any motion to reconsider or modify the calendars previously adopted on January 10, no board member made a motion, leaving Traditional Draft B and Year-Round Draft A unchanged.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting January 24, 2019 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, the January 24, 2019 Durham Public Schools Board of Education meeting centered on 27 public commenters—including Rev. Dr. Fatima Saleh, parents, students, Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People leaders, and DAE educators—protesting punitive in-school suspension (ISS/RPC) practices and stark racial discipline disparities at Durham School of the Arts, prompting DSA Principal Dr. David Hawks to address the board and commit to corrective action. After unanimously approving its amended agenda, November 15, 2018 minutes, and consent agenda (including Budget Amendment #1, chiller replacement, and a Shepard Middle School easement), the board heard a DPS Foundation launch update and NC State OR/Ed's Phase 1 Integrated Planning Study projecting enrollment edging from 32,430 to 32,076 across 113 planned housing developments before agreeing by consensus to enter Phase 2. Following family concerns over non-aligned 2019-20 spring breaks, the board directed staff to return the spring break question to schools for a second vote while unanimously adopting Natalie Beyer's Resolution Supporting Local Control of School Calendars. Finally, the board unanimously approved sending a letter opposing Discovery Charter School state amendments (inviting County Commissioners and City Council to co-sign), met in closed session, and approved the January 24 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Celebrations, and Amended Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened the regular monthly meeting with student/staff recognitions and agenda review. The board voted unanimously by voice vote to amend the agenda by adding Item 11B (2019-20 school calendar review) and Item 12B (letter opposing Discovery Charter School amendments).

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment: Durham School of the Arts Discipline Disparities and School Climate
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Twenty-seven speakers—led by Rev. Dr. Fatima Saleh, students, parents, Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People, and DAE members—presented discipline records and personal testimony alleging excessive, racially disproportionate in-school suspensions (RPC/ISS) for minor infractions at Durham School of the Arts and demanded restorative reforms. DSA Principal Dr. David Hawks also spoke at the podium acknowledging mistakes, committing to listening sessions, and pledging discipline reform.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update, November 15, 2018 Minutes, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga addressed DSA discipline and equity follow-up steps in his Superintendent's Update, after which the board unanimously approved the November 15, 2018 meeting minutes. The board also unanimously approved the consent agenda covering Budget Amendment #1, a chiller replacement contract, and a temporary construction easement at Shepard Middle School.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Minutes and Consent Agenda passed unanimously (Voice)

agenda_items.title: Durham Public Schools Foundation Launch and NC State OR/Ed Integrated Planning Study
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Foundation Chair Jim Key and Executive Director Megan Gonzalez Smith reported initial philanthropic grants and community partnerships supporting district equity initiatives. Next, NC State OR/Ed analysts presented Phase 1 capacity, 113 tracked residential developments, geocoded charter enrollment (~6,700 students), and 10-year public enrollment projections (32,430 declining slightly to 32,076), receiving board consensus to proceed with Phase 2 redistricting and capital analysis.

agenda_items.title: 2019-20 Spring Break Calendar Review and Local Calendar Control Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Responding to public feedback about non-aligned traditional and year-round spring breaks adopted January 10, board members asked administration to survey all schools again specifically on aligning spring break dates. The board then unanimously adopted a Resolution Supporting Local Control of School Calendars urging the General Assembly to lift rigid statutory start/end calendar mandates.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Spring break returned to schools; Resolution passed unanimously (Voice)

agenda_items.title: Opposition Letter on Discovery Charter School Amendments, Closed Session, and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members unanimously approved sending a formal letter to the State Board of Education opposing proposed enrollment/expansion amendments by Discovery Charter School and inviting the Durham County Board of Commissioners and City Council to co-sign. The board then voted unanimously to enter closed session and returned at 03:47:49 to unanimously approve the January 24, 2019 personnel report.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Letter, Closed session, and Personnel report passed unanimously (Voice)

votes.discussion_detail: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved adding Items 11B and 12B to the January 24, 2019 monthly meeting agenda by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 15, 2018 Monthly Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the November 15, 2018 monthly meeting minutes as presented by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Resolution Supporting Local Control of School Calendars
votes.discussion_detail: Following revisions reviewed since January 10, the board unanimously adopted the Resolution Supporting Local Control of School Calendars calling on the North Carolina General Assembly to restore local calendar authority, passing by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Letter to State Board of Education Opposing Discovery Charter School Amendments
votes.discussion_detail: The board unanimously approved sending a letter to the State Board of Education opposing Discovery Charter School expansion/amendment requests and sharing it with the Durham BOCC and City Council for co-signature, passing by voice vote.

votes.discussion_detail: The board unanimously approved entering closed session for personnel and legal matters by voice vote.

votes.discussion_detail: Reconvening in open session at 03:47:49, the board unanimously approved the January 24, 2019 personnel report by voice vote.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Planning Budget Retreat January 17, 2019 4:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education held its January 17, 2019 Budget Planning Retreat to set priorities for the FY 2019-20 budget cycle, voting unanimously at the outset to approve the retreat agenda with no other formal votes taken. CFO Paul LeSieur and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga outlined baseline fiscal pressures, including an initial ~$7.5 million new local funding target, $5 million in recurring strategic plan initiatives originally jump-started with fund balance, $3 million in internal departmental reallocations, rising health/retirement costs, and charter school pass-through transfers. Staff presented initial cost scenarios for certified teacher supplement increases ($1.5 million under Option 2 toward closing gaps with Wake and Chapel Hill-Carrboro), raising classified starting wages toward $13.35/hour alongside Phase 2 of the classified salary study, and adding full-time summer custodians. Board members Dr. Mike Lee, Bettina Umstead, Matt Sears, Natalie Beyer, Steve Unruhe, and Xavier Cason (with five participating in the final breakout table prioritization) weighed priorities around compensation, whole-child student supports, and ongoing facility capital needs.

meetings.title: Durham Board of Education Work Session December 6, 2018 4;30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its December 6, 2018 work session (presided over by Vice Chair Bettina Umstead, with Chair Dr. Mike Lee participating as a board member and staff liaison for the calendar item), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard public comment from Brian Callaway seeking an investigation into the custodial transition, reviewed growth-projection and school-capacity modeling with ITRE Labs ahead of future bond planning, and received a clean 2018 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report audit highlighting rising personnel and charter school pass-through costs. Academic and Student Support Services also presented updates on Lakeview School's trauma-informed redesign and restorative intervention center, as well as instructional and socio-emotional progress at restart schools Glenn Elementary and Lakewood Elementary. The board unanimously approved its agenda, the November 1 work session minutes, three consent items, entering closed session, and the December 6 personnel report, but split 5-1 on a motion by Steve Unruhe (seconded by Minnie Forte-Brown) to cancel the December 20, 2018 board meeting (voice/hand vote; the transcript did not read a roll call naming the single dissenting member or the other three majority voters alongside Unruhe and Forte-Brown). Following closed session, the board also split 4-1 on a motion to amend Paragraph 12 of Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's contract as discussed in closed session (voice/hand vote; the transcript did not read a roll call identifying the four Ayes or the single Nay).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Moment of Silence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board called the December 6, 2018 work session to order and observed a moment of silence.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mike Lee moved and Natalie Beyer seconded approval of the December 6, 2018 work session agenda as presented. The motion passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment on Custodial Transition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Brian Callaway reiterated his November 15 request that the board initiate an investigation into matters surrounding the custodial transition and the accountability structure within the custodial program.

agenda_items.title: Approval of November 1, 2018 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Bettina Umstead moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded approval of the November 1, 2018 board work session minutes. The motion passed by voice vote with no opposition.

agenda_items.title: Consent Items: Hillside Cell Tower, Activity Buses, and Riverside Roof
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented three consent items: a T-Mobile cell tower on a Hillside High School football light pole, year two of the activity bus lease purchase (receiving eight activity buses), and a change order for Riverside High School's roof replacement phase two project. Natalie Beyer moved and Steve Unruhe seconded approval, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Integrated Planning for School and Community & Capacity Modeling
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consultants from ITRE Labs presented an update on integrated planning for school and community and out-of-capacity worksheets, incorporating data from City and County Planning on 117 active or approved development projects in Durham. Discussion noted Durham and Orange counties' leadership in Adequate Public Facility Ordinance coordination and how the modeling informs the next school bond, including a prospective school at Scott King Road, alongside thanks for outgoing facilities leader John Long.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: 2018 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Evan Reeves of Reeves & Associates presented the 2018 CAFR, reporting that 97–98% of the state budget and 74–76% of the total budget goes to salaries, wages, and employee benefits. Benefit costs rose $4.2 million and salaries/wages rose $4.7 million (~$9 million total employee cost increase), charter school payments increased roughly 6.5% even as ADM decreased, and DPS was one of eight NC districts (second largest behind Cabarrus County) to win state financial statement awards under CFO Aaron LeSueur.

agenda_items.title: Additional Public Comment and Lakeview School Redesign & Restorative Practices Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During the mid-meeting public comment window, speaker Amanda Castizo urged strict adherence to district rules, addressed microaggressions toward students of color, and requested immediate parent follow-up on a student case. Dr. Hardy, Dr. Laverne Maddox-Perry, and Lakeview Principal Dr. Theresa McGowan then detailed Lakeview School's six rebranding priorities, including a $50,000 facility/furniture allotment, a second-year trauma-informed partnership with Duke University, a redesigned restorative intervention center replacing traditional in-school suspension, and student-led data conferences.

agenda_items.title: Restart Schools Update: Glenn and Lakewood Elementary
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff updated the board on restart schools Glenn Elementary and Lakewood Elementary, highlighting math and literacy coaches, Eureka Math, Letterland phonics, Glenn's Positivity Project and three Jamaican teacher hires, Lakewood's Capturing Kids' Hearts program and bilingual staff, and plans to evaluate extending the instructional day at both schools with operations and transportation.

agenda_items.title: Cancellation of December 20, 2018 Board Meeting and 2019 Meeting Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mike Lee noted the board had canceled its late-December meeting in the prior two years because no action items were advancing from the work session. Members asked whether canceling would delay teacher hires before the January 4 workday and January 10 meeting (staff offered a phone closed-session option if needed) and discussed correcting irregular January–June 2019 calendar dates in January; Steve Unruhe moved and Minnie Forte-Brown seconded canceling the December 20 meeting, passing 5-1.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items, Closed Session, Personnel Report, and Superintendent Contract Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff noted follow-up items regarding inclement weather impacts, discipline data, and restorative practice updates, after which the board unanimously entered closed session on a motion by Dr. Mike Lee seconded by Natalie Beyer. Returning to open session at 02:47:02, the board unanimously approved the December 6, 2018 personnel report and passed a motion 4-1 to amend Paragraph 12 of Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's contract as discussed in closed session.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed unanimously; Personnel report passed unanimously; Contract amendment passed 4-1

meetings.title: Joint BOCC-BOE Meeting November 20, 2018 9:00 AM
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 20, 2018 joint meeting of the Durham Board of County Commissioners and Durham Public Schools Board of Education (presided over by Dr. Mike Lee), the two boards deferred approval of the August 21 joint meeting minutes for edits and unanimously voted to reorder the agenda to accommodate departing commissioners. Presentations and discussion focused on DPS's enrollment decline of over 600 students alongside charter school growth to 6,957 students, severe elementary classroom capacity pressures from North Carolina's K-3 class-size mandate, and the need for capital planning including two new elementary schools. Staff and Child Care Services Association leaders also presented Durham Pre-K expansion plans, Exceptional Children identification of roughly 350 new preschoolers with disabilities annually, and the new high-school Construction Collaborative apprenticeship pathway with Durham Tech. During public comment, Jovonia Lewis of the Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People requested follow-up on prior community conversations, prompting commitments from both boards to show more clearly how resident feedback shapes budgets and policies. No split votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Deferral of August 21, 2018 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mike Lee called the joint BOCC-BOE meeting to order and led a moment of silence. After a member noted concerns with statements attributed to them in the August 21, 2018 joint meeting minutes and requested time to submit edits, the boards agreed to defer approval of the August 21 minutes until the next joint meeting.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Reordering
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because two county commissioners had to leave after 30 minutes and had already heard the Pre-K study, the boards agreed to move item 4A to the end of the agenda and move item 8 immediately after item 4. A motion to approve the amended agenda passed unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: K-3 Class Size Mandate, Student Enrollment, and Classroom Capacity Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported that DPS enrollment fell by over 600 students in 2018-19 (from 33,181 to 32,520) while charter enrollment rose from 6,506 to 6,957, bringing total Durham County public/charter students to roughly 39,500. Board members and commissioners discussed combination classes, arts and enhancement teachers losing dedicated rooms, trade-offs between kindergarten and Pre-K space at Burton and Merrick-Moore, community access to the Whitted gym, and long-range capital needs to build two new elementary schools and plan redistricting.

agenda_items.title: DPS Pre-K and Exceptional Children Enrollment Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Suzanne Carterman presented DPS Pre-K capacity and Exceptional Children (EC) enrollment data, noting Eno Valley's 45 filled slots across four classrooms and explaining that DPS identifies roughly 350 new preschool children with disabilities each year who must be served. Board members emphasized protecting existing Pre-K capacity despite unfunded K-3 facility pressures.

agenda_items.title: Construction Collaborative Career Pathway Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS staff presented the Construction Collaborative program, embedding high school juniors in three-hour afternoon skilled-trades sessions and moving seniors into paid company apprenticeships with a direct articulation pathway to Durham Tech's two-year construction/project management degree. Board members and commissioners praised the program as a first-choice 'Plan A' option, urged keeping it at Southern High School with strong parent engagement, and asked about student selection.

agenda_items.title: Durham Pre-K Supply and Demand Study & Expansion Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: A representative of Child Care Services Association summarized the county-funded Pre-K supply and demand study and Durham Pre-K expansion following the 2016 early childhood task force. The presentation highlighted gaps for families at Durham's median family income who do not qualify for Head Start, the public-private expansion model, the Pipeline to Pre-K quality-improvement track, and additional Durham Pre-K funding available for Whitted and future DPS classrooms.

agenda_items.title: Public Comment and Community Conversations Follow-Up
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Jovonia Lewis, chair of the education committee for the Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People, asked whether there had been follow-up after community conversations. County and school officials explained that community feedback had been summarized and incorporated into strategic plans and budget priorities, while board members agreed the boards must explicitly communicate back to residents how public input shaped policies and budgets.

votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote of attending BOE and BOCC members; individual mover, seconder, and joint attendance headcount were not read aloud in the transcript.
votes.discussion_detail: Joint boards moved and seconded approving the agenda as amended to move item 4A to the end and item 8 after item 4.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting November 15, 2018 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its November 15, 2018 regular meeting, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously passed the FY 2018-19 $458 million+ budget resolution (reflecting $25 million in adjustments above the spring proposal, $249 million in personnel salaries across 5,003 positions, and rising charter school pass-throughs) as well as the October 18 minutes, closed session, and the November 15 personnel report. During the custodial hiring update, custodians Gloria Howard and Debora Bailey and staff member Brian Callaway raised concerns about pending job offers, alleged retaliation, and requested an independent investigation, while HR reported a 97% rehire rate among contracted custodians and 198 offers made ahead of the December 3 in-house transition. The board's sole split vote occurred on the custodial equipment rebid (about $727,000 split across Sifel Inc., Brame Specialty Co., and Pro-San after downsizing walk-behind scrubbers from 28-inch to 20-inch models to save $159,000), where Matt Sears moved to reject the prior bid, rescind the prior award, and approve the new multi-vendor award. The motion passed 5-2 by voice/hand vote: Sears, Steve Unruhe, Xavier Cason, Bettina Umstead, and Dr. Mike Lee voiced support for rebidding/governance or moved the action, whereas Minnie Forte-Brown and Natalie Beyer objected to splitting the award across three vendors and rebidding after an earlier unanimous award (no formal roll call was read on the 5-2 tally).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened the meeting, introduced interpreter Taneeta Flowers, and led a moment of silence for a seven-year-old bullying suicide victim in Alabama. Celebrations recognized City of Medicine Academy Principal Dr. Tobias (DPS Principal of the Year finalist), Larry McDonald, and 12 student ambassadors to DPAC, followed by Dr. Pascal Mubenga's superintendent update.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the November 15, 2018 meeting agenda as written by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Six public speakers (including Linda Stone and Andrea) addressed two-way dual-language instruction, compliance with federal and state special-needs and ESL laws, concerns over the 'New Direction' alternative placement program lacking teacher coursework, and a proposed nine-experiment STEM program developed by Harvard and MIT students. Dr. Lee asked Dr. Mubenga to arrange a parent meeting.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 18, 2018 Board Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the minutes of the October 18, 2018 Board of Education meeting.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: Pre-K Enrollment and Capacity Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Hardy, Dr. Debbie Pittman, and Suzanne Carterman previewed the Pre-K update for the upcoming joint BOCC-BOE meeting, reporting 50 preschool classrooms serving 817 children (including 133 itinerant EC slots) and 25–26% annual growth (~350 newly identified children) in preschool disability services. Board members pressed for clearer reporting of rolling EC enrollment, separating itinerant community slots from school-based seats, and leveraging the data to secure county Pre-K funding.

agenda_items.title: Human Resources: Custodial Hiring Update and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Custodians Gloria Howard and Debora Bailey described uncertainty over not yet receiving job offers after years of service, and Brian Callaway alleged retaliation against custodial committee advocates and requested an independent law firm investigation. HR Director Arasi Adkins reported 52 of 54 lead custodians hired (11 of 13 DPS leads), all 31 DPS custodians rehired, ~97% (194 of ~200) of contracted custodians recommended, and 198 custodian offers issued with 35 pending before the December 3 in-house start; board members demanded clear communication before the holidays and asked HR to rename 'progressive discipline' training to 'accountability.'

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: FY 2018-19 Budget Resolution
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Aaron LeSueur presented the statutory FY 2018-19 budget resolution totaling over $458 million ($25 million above the spring proposed budget of $432 million), including $8.3 million (1.9%) in fund balance usage, $249 million in personnel salaries across 5,003 positions, and increased charter school pass-through funding. Following board questions on DPS's drop to 32,520 students alongside 6,957 charter students, the board unanimously adopted the budget resolution.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Custodial Equipment Rebid and Prior Award Rescission
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After public comment from Brian Callaway questioning brand-specific bid specifications, staff and legal counsel clarified that DPS had not terminated its Service Solutions contract for convenience (meaning DPS actually retained the option to purchase under-5-year equipment) and recommended rejecting the Nov 1 RFP, rescinding the prior award, and awarding a ~$727,000 low-bid rebid across three vendors (Sifel Inc., Brame Specialty Co., and Pro-San) while switching walk-behind scrubbers from 28-inch to 20-inch to save ~$159,000. Board members sharply debated procurement oversight and multi-vendor logistics before Matt Sears moved to reject the prior bid, rescind the prior award, and approve the rebid, passing 5-2.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and November 15, 2018 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously entered closed session at 03:01:45 and reconvened in open session at 03:26:00, where it unanimously approved the November 15, 2018 personnel report before adjourning.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed unanimously; Personnel report passed unanimously

votes.item_title: Approval of November 15, 2018 Board Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; all seven members present based on subsequent 5-2 board tally.
votes.discussion_detail: Board moved and seconded approving the November 15, 2018 agenda as written.

votes.item_title: Approval of October 18, 2018 Board of Education Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Board moved and seconded approving the October 18, 2018 meeting minutes.

votes.item_title: Approval of FY 2018-19 Budget Resolution ($458M+)
votes.discussion_detail: Board moved and seconded passage of the FY 2018-19 budget resolution under G.S. 115C-425 totaling over $458 million.

votes.item_title: Rejection of Prior Custodial Equipment Bid, Rescission of Prior Award, and Approval of Multi-Vendor Custodial Equipment Rebid
votes.notes: Passed 5-2 by voice/hand vote without a read roll call. In debate, Matt Sears, Steve Unruhe, Xavier Cason, Bettina Umstead, and Dr. Mike Lee expressed support for rebidding or following legal/staff procurement recommendations, while Minnie Forte-Brown and Natalie Beyer spoke critically against rebidding and splitting across three vendors; however, individual Ayes/Nays beyond mover Matt Sears were not announced by roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Matt Sears moved (and an unnamed member seconded) to reject the previous custodial equipment bid, rescind the November 1 award to Brame, and approve the ~$727,000 line-item low-bid rebid split across Sifel Incorporated, Brame Specialty Company, and Pro-San with 20-inch walk-behind scrubbers.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: Moved and seconded to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 15, 2018 Personnel Report
votes.discussion_detail: Upon returning from closed session, the board approved the personnel report dated November 15, 2018.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting November 15, 2018 6:30 PM
disagreements.issue: Custodial Equipment Rebid, Prior Award Rescission, and Multi-Vendor Split
disagreements.summary: The board split 5-2 over rejecting the November 1 custodial equipment RFP award to Brame and approving a ~$727,000 line-item rebid split across Sifel Inc., Brame, and Pro-San following a vendor protest and legal counsel's clarification of contract purchase rights.
disagreements.side_a_position: Rescind the prior award and approve the line-item low-bid rebid across three vendors to ensure statutory compliance, address the vendor protest and prior contract misinterpretation, and maintain transparency on a ~$700k+ purchase.
side_a_arguments: Legal counsel advised rebidding because the original RFP scoring rubric weights and evaluation criteria were not explicitly disclosed to vendors and a formal protest was filed.

Staff corrected an erroneous interpretation of the Service Solutions contract and reduced walk-behind scrubber sizing from 28 inches to 20 inches, saving roughly $159,000 to keep the all-in cost comparable ($727,000 with taxes/fees vs. $689,000 before taxes/fees).
Going back to clarify a major contract after community and vendor scrutiny represents good governance, even while demanding stronger internal contract review going forward.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose rescinding the original award to Brame and splitting equipment purchases across three different vendors at essentially the same total price.
side_b_arguments: Splitting equipment across three vendors (Sifel, Brame, and Pro-San) complicates training, warranties, and maintenance compared to working with a single Durham-based vendor (Brame).

Rebidding delayed implementation ahead of the December 1 in-house transition and spent extra staff and legal time only to arrive at roughly the same price, seemingly driven by fear over a protest rather than substance.
disagreements.resolution: Motion moved by Matt Sears to reject the previous bid, rescind the prior award, and approve the new multi-vendor rebid passed 5-2 by voice/hand vote (without a read roll call).
