meetings.title: Board of Education Work Session November 1, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 1, 2018 work session (presided over by Vice Chair Bettina Umstead in Chair Dr. Mike Lee's absence), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved all ten motions on the agenda, including the October 4 work session minutes, Eastway Elementary chiller replacement and School Improvement Plans on consent, and an amendment clarifying the Dell laptop/Chromebook agreement as a straight lease rather than a lease-purchase. Following community input and board focus on employee equity, the board unanimously adopted the Classified Salary Study priority recommendations for pay grades 50–56 ($500,000 current-year cost, $1.0 million annualized, affecting 600+ employees) and approved Beginning Teacher Support Plan modifications while urging real budget stipends and equity training for school-based mentors. Despite public criticism from Brian Callaway and competing vendor Hank Ballard (Nilfisk) regarding the RFP's 70% non-cost rubric criteria and lack of a full bid tabulation, the board also unanimously approved awarding the custodial equipment RFP to Brame Specialty Company (~$689,000), before reviewing revised inclement weather procedures, Simbli eBoards software, and approving the November 1 personnel report after closed session. No split votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Interpreter Recognition
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Vice Chair Bettina Umstead called the work session to order, led a moment of silence remembering recent shootings in Matthews, NC and Pittsburgh, PA, and introduced Spanish interpreter Taneeta Flowers.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board added a closed-session item prior to item 6 and added an amendment to the Dell lease contract as operational services item 9C. Steve Unruhe moved and Xavier Cason seconded approving the amended agenda, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Approval of October 4, 2018 Work Session Minutes & Brief Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Xavier Cason moved and Steve Unruhe seconded approving the October 4, 2018 work session minutes, passing unanimously. The board then voted unanimously to enter a brief closed session before returning to open session at 00:15:31.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Minutes passed unanimously; Closed session passed unanimously

agenda_items.title: Consent Items: Eastway Chiller Replacement & School Improvement Plans
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Consent items included the Eastway Elementary School chiller replacement bid and annual School Improvement Plans. Steve Unruhe noted concern that state-driven School Improvement Plans had drifted from community participation plans into management documents, then moved approval (seconded by Matt Sears), passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Chief of Staff: Simbli eBoards Software Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Charlie Rigby demonstrated the Simbli eBoards online platform for agenda assembly, searchable meeting minutes, strategic plan tracking, and board visibility controls. Board members expressed interest in stakeholder searchability compared to 200-page PDFs and asked staff to research stakeholder usage in nearby districts before any decision.

agenda_items.title: Human Resources: Classified Salary Study Priority Recommendations (Grades 50–56)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: HR and Finance staff (including Alex Modesto) presented five-year cost projections showing that raising grades 50–56 costs $500,000 in 2018-19 and $1.0 million annualized (covering over half of classified employees, with ~$40,000/year in ongoing retirement/raise escalation). Xavier Cason moved and Minnie Forte-Brown seconded approving the priority recommendations affecting 600+ employees, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Revised Inclement Weather Procedures
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Operational Services presented updated inclement weather protocols establishing target decision deadlines of 8:00 p.m. the night prior and 5:00 a.m. the morning of an event, expanding county-wide road-check assignments, and codifying bus driver tornado/flash-flood procedures after Hurricane Florence and Hurricane Michael. Board members asked staff to post clear summaries online and explore providing bagged meals to students during weather closures or early dismissals.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Custodial Equipment RFP Bid Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Public speakers Brian Callaway and Hank Ballard (Nilfisk) criticized the ~$689,000 custodial equipment RFP for lacking a full bid tabulation, weighting 70% on subjective criteria over low bid (Ballard stated Nilfisk bid ~$592,000), and misstating the Service Solutions contract's buyback option. Staff defended the legal review by Rod Malone and Tharrington Smith, cited Brame Specialty Co.'s superior presentation, quarterly training, and NC school references, and argued Service Solutions had the right to retain under-5-year equipment; Minnie Forte-Brown moved and Xavier Cason seconded awarding the RFP to Brame, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Dell Laptop and Chromebook Lease Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff and legal counsel explained an amendment clarifying that the Dell computer agreement is a straight five-year refresh lease rather than a lease-purchase, avoiding additional statutory hurdles and County Commissioner re-approval so Tharrington Smith can issue its opinion letter. Bettina Umstead moved and Xavier Cason seconded approving the amendment, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Academic & Student Support: Beginning Teacher Support Plan Modifications
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented modifications to the Beginning Teacher Support Plan for state-mandated local board approval, pairing full-release mentors with 1st-year teachers (25–28 caseload) and school-based mentors with 2nd/3rd-year teachers alongside equity-focused mentor training. Several board members (including Steve Unruhe, Matt Sears, and Xavier Cason) urged replacing nominal $200/coffee stipends with meaningful compensation in the upcoming budget cycle and considering REI training; Minnie Forte-Brown moved and Matt Sears seconded approval, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items, Closed Session, and November 1, 2018 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff summarized follow-up items on posting inclement weather timelines, student meal planning during weather closures, vendor outreach, and SIP process improvements. On a motion by Steve Unruhe seconded by Bettina Umstead, the board unanimously entered closed session, and upon returning at 03:25:53 unanimously approved the November 1, 2018 personnel report.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed unanimously; Personnel report passed unanimously

votes.item_title: Approval of Amended November 1, 2018 Work Session Agenda
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Dr. Mike Lee was absent ('some of our colleagues can't be here, especially Mike').
votes.discussion_detail: Steve Unruhe moved and Xavier Cason seconded approving the agenda as modified to add a closed-session item and the Dell contract amendment (item 9C).

votes.item_title: Approval of October 4, 2018 Work Session Minutes
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Dr. Mike Lee absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Xavier Cason moved and Steve Unruhe seconded approval of the October 4, 2018 work session minutes.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Brief Closed Session
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Dr. Mike Lee absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Board voted unanimously to enter a brief closed session for the reasons stated on the amended agenda.

votes.item_title: Approval of Item 6 Consent Items (Eastway Chiller Replacement & School Improvement Plans)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Dr. Mike Lee absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Steve Unruhe moved and Matt Sears seconded approving the consent items (Eastway Elementary chiller replacement bid and School Improvement Plans).

votes.item_title: Approval of Classified Salary Study Priority Recommendations (Grades 50–56)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Dr. Mike Lee absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Xavier Cason moved and Minnie Forte-Brown seconded approving the classified compensation study priority recommendations for grades 50–56 ($500k FY18-19, $1.0M annualized across 600+ employees).

votes.item_title: Approval of Custodial Equipment RFP Award to Brame Specialty Company
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote (later rescinded and rebid on November 15, 2018); Dr. Mike Lee absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Minnie Forte-Brown moved and Xavier Cason seconded accepting the custodial equipment RFP recommendation awarding the ~$689,000 contract to Brame Specialty Company.

votes.item_title: Approval of Amendment to Dell Lease Agreement
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Dr. Mike Lee absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Bettina Umstead moved and Xavier Cason seconded approving the amendment clarifying the Dell computer contract as a straight lease rather than a lease-purchase.

votes.item_title: Approval of Beginning Teacher Support Plan Modifications
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Dr. Mike Lee absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Minnie Forte-Brown moved and Matt Sears seconded accepting the Beginning Teacher Support Plan modifications required under State Board of Education policy.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Dr. Mike Lee absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Steve Unruhe moved and Bettina Umstead seconded entering closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda.

votes.item_title: Approval of November 1, 2018 Personnel Report
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Dr. Mike Lee absent.
votes.discussion_detail: Upon returning from closed session, the board approved the personnel report dated November 1, 2018.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting October 18, 2018 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 18, 2018 regular meeting, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education removed item 13B for attorney review and heard 12 public commenters addressing racial bias in textbooks, college readiness at A+ schools, student mental health, and removing law enforcement from schools. The board unanimously approved the amended agenda, September 20 minutes, consent items (Policy 2015, Eno Valley classroom furniture, and Policy 5080/9040 on drones), and a one-year contract extension for Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga through June 30, 2022 following his positive evaluation. Staff also presented the School Improvement Plan and state-identified low-performing schools framework alongside a comprehensive classified salary study (proposing $500,000 initially for grades 50–56 and $2.0M–$2.5M annualized for full classified alignment, deferred to the November 1 work session for action). Following an hour-long closed session, the board split 5-1 to approve the October 18, 2018 personnel report by voice/hand vote; the transcript did not read a roll call naming the five Aye voters or the single dissenting member.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened the meeting with a moment of silence encouraging early voting, followed by red-carpet recognitions of Riverside High Student of the Month Ray, Fidelity Investments, and community youth partners. Dr. Pascal Mubenga previewed an upcoming grant to establish a skilled-trades academy and noted calendar adjustments following recent inclement weather days.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 13B (a resolution) was removed from the agenda until further discussion with the board's attorney. The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the amended agenda.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Twelve speakers addressed the board, including Pastor Sylvester Williams objecting to a racially offensive caption in a high school evolution textbook, student speakers calling for college-readiness beyond A+ test scores, mental health days, and an undocumented-student scholarship portal, and a Black Youth Project Durham representative urging restorative justice without law enforcement in schools.

agenda_items.title: Approval of September 20, 2018 Minutes & City Water/Durham Bowls Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the September 20, 2018 board minutes. Staff from the City Department of Water Management presented free K–8 conservation contests and a middle school Fix-a-Leak pilot, and School Nutrition reported that all 10 locally chef-developed Durham Bowls recipes will appear on 2019-20 school menus.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: Policy 2015, Eno Valley Furniture, and Policy 5080/9040 (Drones)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The consent agenda included Policy 2015 (Parent and Family Engagement in Title I Programs), a quote for Eno Valley classroom furniture replacement, and second reading of Policy 5080/9040 (Operation of Unmanned Aircraft Systems / Drones). The board unanimously approved all consent items.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: School Improvement Plans and Low-Performing Schools
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Hardy presented the NCStar school improvement planning process, district support teams, instructional coaches, and statutory requirements under G.S. 115C-83.15 for state-identified low-performing schools ahead of November approval. Board members criticized the state's D/F grading formula for failing to reflect student growth or provide funding, and pressed administration to layer racial equity work into school improvement plans.

agenda_items.title: Human Resources: Classified Salary Study Update and Strategic Plan Goal 3
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comment from Antonio Jones urging a $15/hour minimum for all full-time DPS classified employees, HR Director Arasi Adkins and Alex Modesto presented the classified salary study proposing an initial $500,000 allocation from fund balance for grades 50–56 (with $2.0M–$2.5M projected annualized cost in FY 2019-20 for full classified alignment) and scheduled Nov 6 evaluation training for custodial supervisors. The board deferred action on the study to the November 1 work session and also heard a Strategic Plan Goal 3 update on reducing turnover and launching a classified satisfaction survey.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Action deferred to November 1 work session

agenda_items.title: Board of Education: Superintendent's Evaluation and One-Year Contract Extension
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members praised Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's first 11 months of leadership, equity focus, and strategic plan momentum while noting ongoing evaluation goals for improvement. The board unanimously passed a motion offering a one-year contract extension through June 30, 2022, the maximum term allowed under North Carolina law.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and October 18, 2018 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously entered closed session at 03:06:58 and reconvened in open session at 04:10:49. At 04:18:29, a motion to approve the October 18, 2018 personnel report passed 5-1 before adjournment.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed unanimously; Personnel report passed 5-1

votes.discussion_detail: Board moved and seconded approving the October 18, 2018 agenda as amended by removing item 13B for further attorney consultation.

votes.item_title: Approval of September 20, 2018 Board Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Board moved and seconded approving the minutes of the September 20, 2018 monthly meeting.

votes.item_title: One-Year Contract Extension for Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga (Through June 30, 2022)
votes.discussion_detail: Following public remarks on Dr. Mubenga's evaluation and clarification from counsel Ken Soo, a member moved and another seconded extending Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's contract by one year through June 30, 2022.

votes.discussion_detail: Board moved and seconded entering closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda.

votes.notes: Passed 5-1 by voice/hand vote; the transcript did not read a roll call identifying the five Ayes, the single Nay voter, or the mover and seconder.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting October  18, 2018 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: This recording captures the open-session portion of the October 18, 2018 Durham Public Schools Board of Education regular meeting up until the board enters closed session. After removing item 13B for attorney consultation, the board heard 12 public commenters on textbook representation, college readiness at A+ schools, student mental health, and removing law enforcement from schools, and unanimously approved the amended agenda, September 20 minutes, and consent items (Policy 2015, Eno Valley furniture quote, and Policy 5080/9040 on drones). Board members also reviewed School Improvement Plans and state low-performing school rules, deferred action on the classified salary study (initially $500,000 for grades 50–56, with $2.0M–$2.5M projected for full FY 2019-20 alignment) to the November 1 work session, and unanimously voted to extend Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's contract by one year through June 30, 2022 before voting unanimously to enter closed session (where this broadcast stream ends). No split votes occurred within this recording.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Celebrations, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened the meeting with a moment of silence urging residents to vote early, followed by red-carpet recognitions of Riverside High Student of the Month Ray, Fidelity Investments, and community youth partners. Dr. Pascal Mubenga previewed an upcoming skilled-trades academy grant and discussed inclement weather calendar adjustments.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 13B (a resolution) was removed from the agenda pending further attorney review. The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the amended agenda.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Twelve public speakers addressed the board, including Pastor Sylvester Williams regarding a high school evolution textbook caption, student speakers advocating college readiness beyond A+ ratings, mental health support, and an undocumented-student scholarship website, and Black Youth Project Durham advocating restorative justice without school police.

agenda_items.title: Approval of September 20, 2018 Minutes & City Water/Durham Bowls Updates
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the September 20, 2018 board minutes, then heard informational updates from the City Department of Water Management on free K–12 water conservation curricula/contests and from School Nutrition on the Durham Bowls culinary competition putting 10 chef-designed recipes on school menus.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: Policy 2015, Eno Valley Furniture, and Policy 5080/9040 (Drones)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the consent agenda comprising Policy 2015 (Parent and Family Engagement in Title I Programs), a quote for Eno Valley classroom furniture replacement, and second reading of Policy 5080/9040 (Operation of Unmanned Aircraft Systems / Drones).

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: School Improvement Plans and Low-Performing Schools
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Hardy presented the NCStar school improvement planning process and statutory procedures under G.S. 115C-83.15 for state-identified low-performing schools ahead of November work-session approval. Board members criticized North Carolina's school grading formula for undervaluing growth and urged embedding racial equity work across school plans.

agenda_items.title: Human Resources: Classified Salary Study Update and Strategic Plan Goal 3
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following public comment by Antonio Jones advocating a $15/hour minimum for full-time classified staff, HR Director Arasi Adkins and Alex Modesto presented the classified salary study ($500,000 initial fund-balance allocation for grades 50–56; $2.0M–$2.5M annualized projection for FY 2019-20) and Nov 6 evaluation training for custodial supervisors. Action was deferred to the November 1 work session, followed by a Strategic Plan Goal 3 update.

agenda_items.title: Board of Education: Superintendent's Evaluation, Contract Extension, and Closed Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members commended Dr. Pascal Mubenga's performance during his first 11 months and unanimously approved a one-year contract extension through June 30, 2022. The board then voted unanimously to enter closed session at 03:07:23, where this stream ends.

votes.discussion_detail: Board moved and seconded approving the September 20, 2018 meeting minutes.

meetings.title: Operational Services & Policy & Academic Student Services Board Work Session October 4, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At its October 4, 2018 work session, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved adding a presentation from the Durham Association of Educators (DAE), approved the September 6 work session minutes, and passed consent items covering construction and capital planning change orders and Riverside High School roof replacement phase two bids. During general public comment, Brian Callaway alleged demotions and mistreatment of custodial transition committee advocates, while DAE President Bryan Proffitt proposed partnering with HR on building-level morale and launching a building-by-building working conditions survey ahead of the next budget cycle. The board also reviewed ITRE Lab's long-range land-use, student assignment, and magnet evaluation modeling, unanimously advanced first readings of Policy 5080/9040 (Unmanned Aircraft Systems / Drones) and Policy 2015 (Parent and Family Engagement in Title I Programs) to the October monthly consent agenda, and approved the October 4 personnel report as amended following closed session. No split votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Interpreter Recognition, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the work session to order, led a moment of silence, and introduced Spanish interpreter Martha Ramirez. The board unanimously approved adding a Durham Association of Educators presentation between items 6 and 7.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment on Custodial Transition Personnel
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Brian Callaway alleged that members of the three-person custodial transition committee—specifically citing Theo's demotion and Ms. Debora being passed over as a supervisor—faced mistreatment alongside recent job losses.

agenda_items.title: Approval of September 6, 2018 Work Session Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the September 6, 2018 work session minutes.

agenda_items.title: Consent Items: Construction Change Orders and Riverside Roof Bids
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the consent items covering construction and capital planning change order reports and phase two roof replacement bids for Riverside High School.

agenda_items.title: Durham Association of Educators (DAE) Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DAE President Bryan Proffitt proposed three areas of collaboration with DPS: joint planning, a new HR-DAE partnership to address building-level morale concerns, and a comprehensive building-by-building working conditions survey to inform Goal 3 ahead of the upcoming budget cycle. Dr. Pascal Mubenga and board members welcomed the collaboration and requested ideas by December.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: Integrated Planning for School and Community (ITRE Lab)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: ITRE Lab presented its long-range facility planning partnership covering land-use growth modeling, student assignment and boundary analysis, and evaluation of magnet programs. Board members asked staff to integrate community engagement into the later stages of the ITRE process.

agenda_items.title: Policy 5080/9040 (Unmanned Aircraft Systems / Drones) First Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented new Policy 5080/9040 for first reading to establish proactive safety and privacy protections ahead of NCSBA's spring 2019 model policy; board members noted engineering classes currently could not have students operate drones under the 21-year-old restriction and discussed whether to place it on consent or action. The board unanimously voted to place the policy on the next monthly meeting's consent agenda.

agenda_items.title: Policy 2015 (Parent and Family Engagement in Title I Programs) First Reading
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented revisions to Policy 2015 for ESSA compliance, renaming the policy to 'Parent and Family Engagement in Title I Programs' and reinforcing dual-language translation requirements. The board unanimously voted to place the item on the consent agenda for the next monthly meeting after correcting the policy title on the precis.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items, Closed Session, and October 4, 2018 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff noted follow-up items on continuing DAE discussions and integrating community engagement into the ITRE process. The board unanimously voted to enter closed session, returned to open session at 01:54:15, and unanimously approved the October 4, 2018 personnel report as amended.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed unanimously; Personnel report passed unanimously

votes.discussion_detail: Board moved and seconded approving the September 6, 2018 work session minutes.

votes.discussion_detail: Board moved and seconded approving the construction/capital planning change order reports and Riverside High School roof replacement phase 2 bids.

votes.discussion_detail: Board moved and seconded entering closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda.

votes.discussion_detail: Upon returning from closed session, the board approved the personnel report for October 4, 2018 as amended.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting September 20, 2018 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Part 1 of the September 20, 2018 Durham Public Schools Board of Education regular meeting opened with Matt Sears absent in Michigan, Minnie Forte-Brown participating initially by phone from Charlotte before stepping away at 00:38:49, and Xavier Cason joining by phone en route from Raleigh at 01:00:25. Following student and staff celebrations, Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga and staff reviewed the September 17 severe weather response during Hurricane Florence—when 5:00 a.m. road checks cleared buses before sudden flash-flood and tornado warnings forced schools to shelter in place—and committed to a formal postmortem report. The board unanimously approved adding a hurricane pay resolution for non-exempt classified staff to the amended agenda, approved the August 23 minutes, and voted unanimously to reschedule the June 13, 2019 work session to June 6 to avoid high school graduation conflicts, before beginning Strategic Plan and test-score communications presentations where this stream ends.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Attendance Notes, Moment of Silence, and Celebrations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee convened the meeting, noted Matt Sears's absence, Minnie Forte-Brown's remote attendance from Charlotte, and Xavier Cason's planned 7:30 p.m. call-in, and led a moment of silence for five mass shootings in two days. Celebrations recognized the Student of the Month, STEMI Award winner Mr. Davidson, and High School Instructional Assistant of the Year Mr. Barnes.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update on September 17 Inclement Weather Response
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Pascal Mubenga and transportation/operations staff explained the timeline of September 17's post-Florence storm, noting 5:00 a.m. road checks showed safe conditions before flash-flood warnings (8:00–11:15 a.m.) and tornado warnings (7:32–8:00 a.m. and 8:15–8:45 a.m.) required buses to proceed to schools and shelter in place. Board members praised bus drivers and teachers while Dr. Lee confirmed staff would deliver a formal lessons-learned postmortem report; Minnie Forte-Brown stepped off the phone at 00:39:05.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mike Lee introduced Minnie Forte-Brown's request to add a resolution regarding pay for non-exempt classified employees (bus drivers, instructional assistants, cafeteria workers, custodians) affected by hurricane closures as Item 10C before closed session. The board unanimously approved the amended agenda.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Speakers included Kim Harris requesting fulfillment of a court-signed EC settlement agreement for her daughter, Danita Mason-Hogans praising J.D. Clement Early College, Jacqueline Urbano of Latinos Unidos congratulating DPS on rising test scores, an Eno Valley parent objecting to parents being barred from walking first graders to class, and Alexandra suggesting a Latino parent engagement committee.

agenda_items.title: Approval of August 23, 2018 Board Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the August 23, 2018 Board of Education meeting minutes, with Dr. Mike Lee noting that Xavier Cason had joined via phone for the vote.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services: Rescheduling June 2019 Work Session
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff reported a scheduling conflict on June 13, 2019 between the board work session and three high school graduations (9 a.m., 1 p.m., and 5 p.m.). The board unanimously voted to move the June 2019 work session to Thursday, June 6, 2019 at 4:30 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Academic Services & Public Affairs: Strategic Plan and Test Score Communications
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Hardy outlined the five strategic plan priorities, goal team leadership, and quarterly board update schedule (Oct, Jan, Mar, May, and year-end). Public Affairs Director Chip Sudderth then began explaining how his reorganized team worked to publicize 2017-18 K–8 academic gains despite local newsroom cuts, with this video stream ending mid-presentation at 01:17:10.

votes.item_title: Approval of Amended September 20, 2018 Agenda (Adding Item 10C Hurricane Pay Resolution)
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote among the four members present at that time (Matt Sears was absent in Michigan, Xavier Cason had not yet called in, and Minnie Forte-Brown stepped off the phone at 00:39:05).
votes.discussion_detail: Board moved and seconded adding the hurricane pay resolution for non-exempt classified staff as Item 10C and approving the amended agenda.

votes.item_title: Approval of August 23, 2018 Board of Education Minutes
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote (5-0; Sears absent, Forte-Brown off line).
votes.discussion_detail: Board moved and seconded approving the August 23, 2018 meeting minutes, with Xavier Cason participating by phone.

votes.item_title: Move June 2019 Work Session from June 13 to June 6, 2019
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote (5-0; Sears absent, Forte-Brown off line).
votes.discussion_detail: Board moved and seconded rescheduling the June 13, 2019 work session to June 6, 2019 at 4:30 p.m. to avoid conflicting with three high school graduations.

meetings.title: Operational Services & Policy & Academic Student Services Board Work Session September 6, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At its September 6, 2018 work session (opened while Chair Dr. Mike Lee joined initially by phone before arriving in person, with Spanish interpretation provided by ESL teacher Martha Gintzma-Ramirez), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved its agenda, minutes, and a three-item operational consent agenda that terminated the prior Northern High School replacement design contract to clear the way for a new contract at the next meeting. Academic leadership led by Dr. Nakia Hardy, Dr. Julie Spencer, and Crystal Ball presented state ESSA accountability results showing proficiency gains alongside board requests for cohort analysis and disaggregated data, followed by an update from Dr. Debbie Pittman and Dr. McGowan on restorative and arts-integrated programming at Lakeview School. The board unanimously approved continuing the Alternative Schools Progress Model for 2018-19 for Lakeview School and the Performance Learning Center, and unanimously approved the roughly $13 million 2018-19 Title I District Plan and Planning Allotment after questioning CFO Paul LeSieur on post-allotment spending transparency. After entering closed session, the board returned to open session and unanimously approved the September 6, 2018 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Interpreter Introduction, Agenda Approval, Minutes, and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a brief delay while members traveled in traffic and Chair Dr. Mike Lee initially joined by phone, the board opened the meeting, introduced Spanish interpreter Martha Gintzma-Ramirez, and held a moment of silence. The board unanimously approved the agenda, confirmed no general public comment sign-ups while keeping the floor open for latecomers, approved prior meeting minutes, and adopted three operational consent items: terminating the Northern High School replacement design contract so a new contract could move forward, and receiving information on the five-year technology refresh plan and Microsoft Ed license agreement.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Agenda, Minutes, and Consent Agenda each passed unanimously (Voice)

agenda_items.title: ESSA State Accountability Results Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and Dr. Julie Spencer presented the district's ESSA accountability results, covering English learner progress, End-of-Grade and End-of-Course school performance grades, Math 1 and upcoming Math 3 middle school testing rules, and districtwide proficiency gains. Board members welcomed growth improvements (from 1.5 to 1.9) while requesting cohort analyses to track third-grade reading dips and disaggregated results for public review.

agenda_items.title: Lakeview School 2018-19 Program Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following May 2018 revisions to Policy 4303 converting Lakeview School to disciplinary reassignment as an alternative to long-term suspension, Dr. Debbie Pittman and Dr. McGowan outlined 2018-19 priorities anchored in Strategic Plan Priority 2. Updates included restorative practices, conflict resolution and social-emotional learning, hiring a full-time arts teacher for middle and high school, university math tutoring, and a Department of Social Services partnership implementing the NC ePASS system for family benefits.

agenda_items.title: 2018-19 Alternative School Accountability Model
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julie Spencer and Director of State Assessments and Accountability Crystal Ball recommended continuing the state's Alternative Schools Progress Model for both the Performance Learning Center and Lakeview School for the 2018-19 school year. The board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the recommendation.

agenda_items.title: 2018-19 Title I District Plan and Planning Allotment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Dietrich Danner presented the 2018-19 Title I District Plan and ~$13 million planning allotment, noting Carrington, Githens, and Lucas were newly added to Title I, 12 schools qualified under the Community Eligibility Provision, and funds supported 33 literacy and math coaches, school improvement interventions ($1,075,023.12), and professional development ($646,475.55). Board members questioned CFO Paul LeSieur on non-personnel budget size and asked for post-allotment actual spending reports before unanimously approving the planning allotment.

agenda_items.title: Announcements, Follow-Up Summary, Closed Session, and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: HR Director Atkins announced an upcoming custodial job fair posted on the district website, and staff checked once more for general public comment and summarized follow-up requests (disaggregated data, cohort analysis, consideration of renaming Lakeview School, and post-allotment Title I spending). The board voted unanimously to enter closed session and, upon returning to open session at 02:20:25, unanimously approved the September 6, 2018 personnel report.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session and Personnel report each passed unanimously (Voice)

votes.item_title: Approval of September 6, 2018 Work Session Agenda
votes.notes: Unanimous voice vote; Chair Dr. Mike Lee was initially connected by phone while arriving in person.
votes.discussion_detail: A board member moved and another seconded approving the September 6, 2018 work session agenda as presented. The motion passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Board Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Board members moved and seconded approval of the prior board meeting minutes with no modifications. Passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of 2018-19 Alternative Schools Progress Model
votes.discussion_detail: Following the presentation by Dr. Julie Spencer and Crystal Ball, a board member moved to support the administration's recommendation to continue the Alternative Schools Progress Model for Lakeview School and the Performance Learning Center in 2018-19. Passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of 2018-19 Title I District Plan and Planning Allotment
votes.discussion_detail: Following Dr. Dietrich Danner's presentation and board questions on post-allotment spending tracking, a board member moved approval of the district Title I planning allotment for 2018-19. Passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: A board member moved and another seconded entering closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda. Passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.discussion_detail: After returning to open session, Chair Dr. Mike Lee called for a motion on the personnel report dated September 6, 2018 as discussed in closed session. Moved, seconded, and passed unanimously by voice vote.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting August 23, 2018 6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 23, 2018 regular monthly meeting presided over by Chair Dr. Mike Lee, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education recognized its August Student of the Month from Middle College High School and DPS deaf and hard-of-hearing educators before hearing Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga's reflections on the district's convocation. Celebrations honored the August Student of the Month from Middle College High School (introduced by Principal Marcia Navarro) and DPS deaf and hard-of-hearing teachers, after which Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga thanked Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni and staff for the convocation.

agenda_items.title: Approval of July 10, 2018 Special Called Organizational Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board reviewed the July 10, 2018 special called organizational meeting minutes and approved them unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Academic Services brought forward an NCASCD Whole Child resolution and led an upstander kindness pledge, followed by Rick Sheldon's Career and Technical Education (CTE) update covering pathways, four-year career planning, Scholars at Work ($100 stipends for 85 students), 200 citywide summer interns (including 40 within DPS and 25 at the Hub Farm), Durham Tech alignment, and AJ Fletcher Foundation support. meetings.title: Operational Services & Policy & Academic Student Services Board Work Session August 9, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At its August 9, 2018 work session (the first meeting of the 2018-19 academic year), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard public comment from Duke University Program in Education leaders praising PK-12 partnerships and from a 25-year custodial veteran protesting reapplication requirements and potential demotions after budget cuts. The board unanimously approved its agenda, June 14, 2018 minutes, and consent items (Budget Amendment No. 3 and Insurance Renewal Program Overview), and voted unanimously on a motion by Minnie Forte-Brown (seconded by Natalie Beyer) to allocate $70,000 in one-time fund balance money so the newly organized DPS Foundation could hire an executive director. Members also reviewed options for the annual superintendent evaluation instrument—comparing the packet form with a more data-heavy subcommittee form brought by Natalie Beyer—before a mid-meeting gap in the digest. Later in the session, the board unanimously waived second reading to adopt revised Policies 4301 (Code of Student Conduct for elementary and middle/high schools) and 4303 (Suspension and Expulsion) ahead of school opening, unanimously approved 2018-19 K-12 curriculum and assessment purchase agreements (Curriculum Associates, Discovery Education, Learning A-Z, Reading Plus, Carnegie Learning, and TE21), and approved the August 9 personnel report after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board convened its first work session of the academic year at 4:34 p.m. and observed a moment of silence for DPS students. Members unanimously approved the agenda as printed.

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Duke University Program in Education Chair Susan Nguyen and colleague Naomi Croutt thanked DPS for PK-12 and Durham Teaching Fellows partnerships and invited board members to a September 25 reception. A 25-year veteran custodial employee who served 13 years as an inspector until budget cuts spoke forcefully against requiring veteran staff to reapply for positions subject to principal approval, warning of demotions and pay cuts.

agenda_items.title: Approval of June 14, 2018 Minutes and Consent Items (Budget Amendment No. 3 and Insurance Renewal)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On a motion by Dr. Mike Lee seconded by Natalie Beyer, the board unanimously approved the June 14, 2018 work session minutes. On a motion by Minnie Forte-Brown seconded by Dr. Mike Lee, the board also unanimously approved two consent items: Budget Amendment No. 3 and the Insurance Renewal Program Overview.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Minutes and Consent items each passed unanimously (Voice)

agenda_items.title: DPS Foundation One-Time Director Funding ($70,000)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Administration reported positive meetings with DPS Foundation Chair Jim Key and foundation board members who had developed a vision, mission, and goals. Minnie Forte-Brown moved and Natalie Beyer seconded allocating a one-time $70,000 fee from fund balance so the foundation could hire its executive director immediately, which passed unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent Evaluation Instrument Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Mike Lee introduced the annual superintendent evaluation process and packet form, while Natalie Beyer distributed an alternative instrument developed by a board subcommittee three to four years earlier that added a data-heavy academic section alongside an almost identical qualitative section. Members discussed aligning targets with the strategic plan, whether to evaluate in August or September after seven to eight months of Dr. Mubenga's tenure, and having staff rather than only the Chair and Vice Chair tally scores.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / No vote recorded in digest

agenda_items.title: Waiver of Second Reading and Approval of Policies 4301 and 4303
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming during discussion of disciplinary reassignment and restorative justice, board members urged that reassignment remain a last resort rather than heavy-handed, while Dr. Nakia Hardy affirmed principals treat it as a last resort ensuring continuous social-emotional and academic support. Because traditional schools were about to open, Dr. Mike Lee moved and Minnie Forte-Brown seconded waiving second reading and immediately approving Policy 4301 (Code of Student Conduct - Elementary), Policy 4301 (Code of Student Conduct - Middle and High Schools), and Policy 4303 (Suspension and Expulsion), passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: 2018-19 Academic Services Instructional and Assessment Purchase Agreements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Executive Director for K-12 Curriculum and Instruction Ms. Sidberry presented 2018-19 vendor contracts aligned with Strategic Plan Priority 1, including Curriculum Associates (i-Ready/Teacher's Toolbox), Discovery Education, Learning A-Z, Reading Plus (expanded to incoming freshmen with reading deficits), Carnegie Learning (in-classroom math PD for grades 6-12), and TE21 (expanded districtwide K-12). Dr. Mike Lee moved and Steve Unruhe seconded approving the purchase agreements, passing unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Summary, Closed Session, and August 9 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Members noted a September work session follow-up on alternative schools and a separate update from Dr. Mubenga before voting unanimously to enter closed session. Returning to open session at 03:20:05, the board unanimously approved the August 9, 2018 personnel report and adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session and Personnel report each passed unanimously (Voice)

votes.item_title: Approval of August 9, 2018 Work Session Agenda
votes.discussion_detail: Board members moved and seconded approving the August 9, 2018 work session agenda as printed. Passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of June 14, 2018 Work Session Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Dr. Mike Lee and seconded by Natalie Beyer to approve the June 14, 2018 work session minutes. Passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of Consent Items (Budget Amendment No. 3 and Insurance Renewal Program Overview)
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Minnie Forte-Brown and seconded by Dr. Mike Lee to approve Budget Amendment No. 3 and the Insurance Renewal Program Overview on consent. Passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of $70,000 One-Time Fund Balance Allocation for DPS Foundation Executive Director
votes.discussion_detail: Minnie Forte-Brown moved and Natalie Beyer seconded authorizing a one-time $70,000 fee from fund balance for the DPS Foundation to hire an executive director, emphasizing it is non-recurring seed support. Passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Waiver of Second Reading and Adoption of Policies 4301 (Elementary & Middle/High Code of Student Conduct) and 4303 (Suspension and Expulsion)
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Dr. Mike Lee and seconded by Minnie Forte-Brown to waive second reading due to imminent school opening and approve Policy 4301 (Elementary Code of Student Conduct), Policy 4301 (Middle and High School Code of Student Conduct), and Policy 4303 (Suspension and Expulsion). Passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of 2018-19 Academic Services Purchase Agreements (Curriculum Associates, Discovery Education, Learning A-Z, Reading Plus, Carnegie Learning, TE21)
votes.discussion_detail: Moved by Dr. Mike Lee and seconded by Steve Unruhe to approve the 2018-19 academic services purchase agreements presented by Ms. Sidberry. Passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: Board members moved and seconded entering closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda. Passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of August 9, 2018 Personnel Report
votes.discussion_detail: Returning to open session, the board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the August 9, 2018 personnel report as discussed in closed session.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools BOE Organizational Meeting and Swearing-In Ceremony July 10, 2018
meetings.executive_summary: At its July 10, 2018 special called organizational meeting and swearing-in ceremony, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education passed the gavel to Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga so the four newly re-elected board members could take their oaths of office together before approving the agenda. Following Policy 2200 officer election procedures, the board unanimously re-elected Dr. Mike Lee as Chair and unanimously elected Steve Unruhe as Vice Chair. Chair Lee delivered remarks highlighting district progress over the prior four years—including over $50 million in student scholarships ($20 million at Hillside alone), fighting state takeover, and expanding AIG identification for Black and Brown students—and urging collective focus on the new Strategic Plan with Dr. Mubenga. After entering closed session, the board reconvened in open session and unanimously approved the July 10, 2018 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Swearing-In of Re-Elected Members, and Agenda Approval
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the organizational meeting to order, led a moment of silence, and passed the gavel to Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga. After confirming the four re-elected members should be sworn in before voting on the agenda, Dr. Mubenga administered the oath of office to them jointly, and the board then unanimously approved the agenda.

agenda_items.title: Election of Board Chair and Vice Chair (Policy 2200) and Chair's Remarks
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Under Policy 2200 procedures, Dr. Mubenga opened nominations for Chair; Dr. Mike Lee was nominated and elected unanimously, resuming the gavel. Chair Lee then opened nominations for Vice Chair, and Steve Unruhe was nominated and elected unanimously, after which Lee delivered a four-minute speech celebrating $50 million in scholarships, AIG equity gains, resisting state takeover, and launching the Strategic Plan era with Dr. Mubenga.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Chair and Vice Chair elections each passed unanimously (Voice)

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and July 10, 2018 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted unanimously to enter closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda. Returning to open session at 00:58:04, the board unanimously approved the July 10, 2018 personnel report presented by Dr. Mubenga and adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session and Personnel report each passed unanimously (Voice)

votes.item_title: Approval of July 10, 2018 Organizational Meeting Agenda
votes.discussion_detail: Following the swearing-in ceremony for re-elected board members, the board moved and approved the organizational meeting agenda unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Election of Dr. Mike Lee as Board Chair
votes.discussion_detail: Dr. Pascal Mubenga presided over the Chair election under Policy 2200 (nominations require no second). Dr. Mike Lee was the sole nominee and was elected unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Election of Steve Unruhe as Board Vice Chair
votes.discussion_detail: Chair Dr. Mike Lee opened nominations for Vice Chair; a board member nominated Steve Unruhe, and with no other nominations, the board elected him unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: A board member moved and another seconded entering closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda. Passed unanimously by voice vote.

votes.item_title: Approval of July 10, 2018 Personnel Report
votes.discussion_detail: Reconvening in open session, the board moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the July 10, 2018 personnel report as discussed in closed session.

meetings.search_blob: durham public schools boe organizational meeting and swearing-in ceremony july 10, 2018 dr. mike lee at its july 10, 2018 special called organizational meeting and swearing-in ceremony, the durham public schools board of education passed the gavel to superintendent dr. pascal mubenga so the four newly re-elected board members could take their oaths of office together before approving the agenda. following policy 2200 officer election procedures, the board unanimously re-elected dr. mike lee as chair and unanimously elected steve unruhe as vice chair. chair lee delivered remarks highlighting district progress over the prior four years—including over $50 million in student scholarships ($20 million at hillside alone), fighting state takeover, and expanding aig identification for black and brown students—and urging collective focus on the new strategic plan with dr. mubenga. after entering closed session, the board reconvened in open session and unanimously approved the july 10, 2018 personnel report. governance & transparency staff compensation & labor call to order, swearing-in of re-elected members, and agenda approval election of board chair and vice chair (policy 2200) and chair's remarks closed session and july 10, 2018 personnel report approval of july 10, 2018 organizational meeting agenda election of dr. mike lee as board chair election of steve unruhe as board vice chair motion to enter closed session approval of july 10, 2018 personnel report
